| [09 — The palettes](docs/09-the-palettes.md) | fourteen files, one of them twice, and a base index nobody wrote down |
| [10 — Where I stopped](docs/10-where-i-stopped.md) | 14.392 % of this object does not state its own length |
| [11 — The Germans](docs/11-the-germans.md) | a keyboard, nineteen names, and one line the font cannot draw |
| [12 — Fifty-five bytes](docs/12-fifty-five-bytes.md) | somebody played this, and left the evidence |
| [13 — One clock](docs/13-one-clock.md) | and its three weaknesses, stated first rather than discovered |
| [14 — Against the collection](docs/14-against-the-collection.md) | zero of 23,631, and how to make a zero informative |
| [15 — The byte account](docs/15-the-byte-account.md) | the first honest attempt at "how much of this do we know" |
| [16 — Open questions](docs/16-open-questions.md) | seven open, and eight that no folder can ever ask |
| [17 — The scoring](docs/17-prediction-scoring.md) | 25 / 8 / 7 / 1, and method beats content 85 % to 46 % |
| [18 — The tools](docs/18-tools.md) | 167 scripts, and the 112 with nothing to open |
| [19 — Leftovers](docs/19-leftovers.md) | 9,043 bytes, and the chapter the briefing expected to be the biggest |
| [20 — Corrections](docs/20-corrections.md) | four errors in the briefing, seven of mine |

---

## The five things worth knowing

**One — a folder cannot date itself, and that is the finding.** Twelve subjects
in a row carried a notary: an ISO 9660 volume descriptor states when the volume
was built, by what program, and where it stops. A directory tree carries only
its members' own timestamps, restored by whatever last copied them. What a
folder *can* prove is completeness and internal consistency, and both were
proved here: 106 of 107 files reachable from `TUBWORLD.BAT` with nothing spare
and nothing missing, and every one of the 107 timestamps on the MS-DOS
two-second grid with a zero sub-second field. What it cannot prove is its own
manufacture, and [chapter 16](docs/16-open-questions.md) writes that down as the
opening question for every future session without a medium.

**Two — the whole game is drawn from a 64-byte tile.** Seven of the fifteen tile
banks are exact multiples of 64 once 768 bytes of VGA palette come off the end,
and the tile indices across all twenty-one maps form the dense range **0..2639**
with every gap equal to one. That caps the tile at 65 bytes, which forces 64,
which is 8 × 8 at one byte per pixel. Rendered, `MAP9A.DAT` reads **GET READY**
and `MAP9D.DAT` reads **GAME OVER** — two files whose contents nothing in the
executables names, decoded from arithmetic.

**Three — a closed form that holds thirty-five times, and the two that break it
agree.** `size = w·h·k + 4` on every level grid, with the map and the object
grid of each level declaring the same width and height, sixteen times out of
sixteen. Level 3 breaks it in both files with the identical bytes `a9 00 30 00`.
The briefing read that as a wrong header and it is not: the autocorrelation
peaks at **169** and is at chance at 200, the level renders coherently at 169 and
shears at 200, and the content stops at exactly the row the header declares.
**The header is right and the file is 1,488 cells too long** — in both members
of the pair.

**Four — a German keyboard, forced by two scancodes and not one.** Fifty-eight
bytes compiled into both game programs, indexed by IBM scancode from zero: `1`
at 0x02, `Q` at 0x10, `A` at 0x1E, `M` at 0x32, a space at 0x39. And **`Z` at
0x15 and `Y` at 0x2C**, which are the two positions a US layout has the other
way round. Nobody wrote that down to tell anybody anything; it is in a lookup
table because of the keyboard on somebody's desk.

**Five — 85.447 % structured, 74.383 % decoded, 0.263 % leftover.** Twelve
600 MB discs could not publish that honestly. At 3.4 MB it can be checked, and
the tiers were defined in the predictions before any of them was counted. The
14.392 % that is neither is `.SHP` and `.ZMP` exactly — the two formats that do
not state their own length — and
[chapter 10](docs/10-where-i-stopped.md) says where the measuring stopped and
why.

---

## Reproducing it

No drive is involved. Everything here comes from 107 files on disc.

    python tools/foldercensus.py TubularWorlds --tsv notes/tree.tsv
    python tools/refgraph.py TubularWorlds
    python tools/mz.py TubularWorlds
    python tools/sharedcode.py TubularWorlds/PART1.EXE TubularWorlds/PART2.EXE
    python tools/sharedcode.py TubularWorlds/PART1.EXE TubularWorlds/CHECKMS.EXE
    python tools/ilbm.py TubularWorlds/LG01.DAT --ppm _work/lg01.ppm
    python tools/ilbm.py TubularWorlds/LG02.DAT --ppm _work/lg02.ppm
    python tools/mapobj.py TubularWorlds/TEDIT
    python tools/anim.py TubularWorlds/TEDIT/ANIM
    python tools/col.py TubularWorlds
    python tools/hof.py TubularWorlds
    python tools/tilecensus.py TubularWorlds
    python tools/explained.py TubularWorlds

    # the renders that refuted or confirmed the tile model
    python tools/vgatiles.py --bank TubularWorlds/TEDIT/CHAR/CHAR99.VGA \
        --sheet _work/char99.png --cols 20 --scale 6
    python tools/vgatiles.py --bank TubularWorlds/TEDIT/CHAR/CHAR97.VGA \
        --map TubularWorlds/TEDIT/MAP/MAP9A.DAT --out _work/map9a.png --scale 2
    python tools/vgatiles.py --bank TubularWorlds/TEDIT/CHAR/CHAR97.VGA \
        --map TubularWorlds/TEDIT/MAP/MAP9D.DAT --out _work/map9d.png --scale 2
    python tools/vgatiles.py --bank TubularWorlds/TEDIT/CHAR/CHAR00.VGA \
        --palette TubularWorlds/SCON/COL/LEVEL0.COL --prefix 0 \
        --map TubularWorlds/TEDIT/MAP/MAP0A.DAT --out _work/map0a.png

    python tools/strdump.py TubularWorlds/PART2.EXE --min 5
    python tools/strdump.py TubularWorlds/PART2.EXE --accent

    python tools/hashall.py TubularWorlds > notes/sha1-all.txt
    python tools/fivelists.py --show-matches
    python tools/stringcross.py

    # before committing
    python tools/checklinks.py
    python tools/toolclass.py
    python tools/checkscore.py docs/17-prediction-scoring.md

`TubularWorlds/` holds the material and `_work/` holds the renders. Neither is
in this repository and neither ever will be: **nothing here contains a byte of
the object's content.** The saved output of every run above is in `notes/`.

---

## What this repository is part of

One of a family of measurement repositories indexed at
[pc-gamelist-doc](https://github.com/vs-sr-dev/pc-gamelist-doc). The published
hash lists of the other subjects are what
[chapter 14](docs/14-against-the-collection.md) compares against, and this one
contributes `notes/sha1-all.txt`, 107 files. It has no second list: there is no
Macintosh catalogue here and no resource fork, so nothing is invisible to a PC
and nothing is missing from that list.

# pc-polanie-doc

A measured description of one folder: 90 files, 14,957,416 bytes, as one
ZIP delivered them, holding **POLANIE** (MS-DOS, `ver. 1.1  marzec 1996`,
printed by its own program; no company named anywhere in it; nine people
credited in a text file) — a Polish build-and-raid strategy set among the
Slavic tribes, sold here as *Slavs*, "the DOS base version in English".
Three quarters of the bytes are one animation; a tenth is music that is
94 % hidden copies of the program; the game is under 8 %, and its English
is a memory-resident patch of 59 strings. The object is not published.
What is published is what could be counted, unpacked, decoded, rendered
and checked — all of it read out of the object's own bytes, none of it
from outside.

## The short card

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **what it is** | a top-down strategy of villages, cows and raids across tenth-century Poland: six building types, nine unit types a side, one resource (**milk**, capped per level), an enemy with four algorithms, 28 maps of 66 × 66 tiles with English briefings — the designers' own legend at the end of the level file says so; delivered as one 15 MB folder of which **74 % is a 26-second title animation and 8.8 % is eighteen keyed copies of the engine hidden in the music** |
| **title** | POLANIE — the banner `P O L A N I E` in the unpacked engine, `polanie.exe` ×3, the word carved in stone in the animation's last ninety frames and under the menu's spears; *Slavs* is what the English TSR writes over the banner and the release's file name |
| **studio** | *(none named)* — the credits in `LEVEL.INI`, in the Mazovia code page: coders Mirosław Dymek, Artur Bidziński, Lidia Dutkiewicz; music Marcin "Red" Adamowicz; history Andrzej Kwaśniewski, Maciej Janiec; graphics Paweł Chwaleba, Beata Brzuchacz, M. Dymek; levels L. Dutkiewicz, Bartłomiej Piwek, M. Dymek; the project folder `!POLANIE` on a drive `C:\GRAFIKA` inside the animation |
| **year** | 1996 — `marzec 1996` (March) printed by the engine; the animation's own stamp 1996-02-26; the modules 1996-02-26, the levels 02-29, the engine 03-05; the translation TSR says `1996` and rewrites the month to `sept.`, the batch is 1996-09-09 |
| **language** | Polish end to end — the engine's every string, the font (ą ę ó ź ś ć ł on `# $ % & * + \``), the menu, the difficulty selector, the map; English only in `CRACK.COM`'s 59 same-length replacements and in 24 of 25 written briefings (level 3 is still Polish); nothing German |
| **platform** | IBM PC, 386, VGA 320 × 200 × 256, mouse, EMS 4.0, 586 KB low memory; AdLib/OPL2 music (Scream Tracker 3.20, 100 FM patches, 0 samples), 55 PCM 8-bit 22 kHz sounds; Borland C++ 1991 |
| **files** | 90 in 2 directories: 1 FLC, 19 `GRAF.0xx` (18 S3M + 1 not), 55 WAV, 6 pictures + 2 palettes, 1 level file + 1 text file, 3 packed programs + 1 FLC player, 1 TSR, 1 batch, 7 bytes of settings |
| **bytes** | 14,957,416 — animation 11,090,932 (74.1501 %), "music" 1,388,657 (9.2841 %, of which modules 78,329 and engine copies 1,309,824), sounds 999,758 (6.6840 %), pictures 1,086,658 (7.2650 %), levels + text 141,003, programs 172,496, the rest 77,912 (`GRAF.019`, palettes, the TSR, the batch, the settings) |
| **distinct sha1** | 85 — four groups of identical WAVs |
| **the clocks** | seven: 1996 on 23 files and in three printed places; 2096-02-28 01:00:00 on 66 (one event, year field 116); 2009-12-25 on the repackager's four; 1993 in the FLC player; 1991 and 1990 in the compilers' banners |
| **coverage** | specified 92.2144 %, derived 7.2788 % (the pictures, the TSR), opaque 0.5068 % (`GRAF.019`, two palettes, 7 bytes), residue 0 — from 91.2838 % opaque before this session |
| **the program** | `SLAVS.EXE` 72,768 B behind a packer no table names: a 1,415-byte stub read whole (626 instructions, 100 % decoded), `dataarea.py` written from it, 180,712 B unpacked with the original header verbatim, 3,002 relocations all inside; `SETUP.EXE` and `PLAYER.EXE` the same stub, the same closure |
| **the animation** | `SWIAT.DAT`, Animator Pro FLC, 372 frames walked to the byte, one palette, one shot: a 3D camera around the four-faced stone idol (Światowid) ending on POLANIE carved in stone; 1 frame damaged in the file (85) |
| **the pictures** | 34 images with a 6-byte head whose second word is the stride, **319**, not 320 (the first render was skewed and the owner said so); `GRAF.DAT` 30 slots → 15 screens of 319 × 201: menu, campaign map of Poland, idol at night, the offering, sprite sheets; 14 palettes at 8 bits, 11 distinct |
| **the levels** | 28 text maps with the designers' Polish legend; 122,034 cells, 91.12 % in the legend; 230 of our units, 734 of theirs; 30 briefings, 30 victories, 30 defeats, the start, the ending, the credits |
| **the hidden program** | every `.S3M` = 1–12 KB of module + `SLAVS.EXE` under a 20-byte additive key (0 mismatches ×18); `GRAF.012` holds the 18-record index |
| **the "crack"** | `CRACK.COM`, `JdA/RLX 1996`, a packed TSR unpacked by `comunpack.py` from its own stub: **the English edition** — 59 Polish→English pairs, `P O L A N I E` → `S L A V S`, `marzec` → `sept.` |
| **crossings** | 0 of 85 over 115 repositories |
| **tools** | 598 Python files: 592 inherited (1 changed), 6 written |

**The work this time was three readers and an unpacker, and the object
kept answering with more than was asked.** The packer's stub was
disassembled to the last of 1,415 bytes and `dataarea.py` written from the
listing; out came the title, the month, the Polish interface and the four
tribes. The animation's 128-byte header got the one branch it needed and
372 frames walked to residue 0; out came a stone god and the title carved
under it. The pictures' six-byte head was read, rendered, corrected by the
owner's eye from 320 to 319, and rendered again; out came the menu, the
map of Poland and the offering table. The level file was split into 28 and
its own legend — milk, cows, four enemy algorithms — read at the end of the
file; the text file gave up the credits in a code page nobody had named.
And then the two files nobody expected anything of: eighteen music modules
each carrying the whole program under a key, and a "crack" that, unpacked,
is the English translation, string for string, same length each.

**The pre-briefing was wrong fourteen times**, each caught by a byte, from
27 levels that are 28 to a crack that is the edition. Its five hunches
score one true and four halves.

## The chapters

Eight, and the count is the content's. One for the program, because the
packer is the gate to the words; one for the animation, because it is
74 %; one for the pictures, because their stride was wrong until a person
looked; one for the levels, because the game is legible there without a
disassembler; one for the music, the sounds, the hidden program and the
translation together, because they are one story about integrity and a
TSR; and one for the clocks, the crossings and the scoring.

| chapter | the sentence |
|---|---|
| [01 — What this is](docs/01-what-this-is.md) | a 15 MB strategy of which three quarters is one animation and the game is under 8 %: the object, the split, what it says about itself, the denominators, the coverage, the two cells |
| [02 — The technical sheet](docs/02-the-technical-sheet.md) | every figure with the command that re-derives it |
| [03 — The program](docs/03-the-program.md) | a packer with no name, read from its stub and removed; the banner, the month, the Polish words, the tribes, the two other programs |
| [04 — The animation](docs/04-the-animation.md) | 372 frames of a stone idol and the title, one palette, one shot, one damaged frame, and the developer's drive inside the prefix |
| [05 — The pictures](docs/05-the-pictures.md) | thirty-four images at stride 319, fifteen screens, fourteen palettes ranked by fit, and a font with Polish on the punctuation |
| [06 — The levels](docs/06-the-levels.md) | twenty-eight maps, the designers' legend, milk, the briefings in two languages, the credits in Mazovia, the genre measured |
| [07 — The music, the sounds, the hidden program and the translation](docs/07-the-music-the-sounds-the-hidden-program-and-the-translation.md) | eighteen AdLib modules each carrying the engine under a key, the index, fifty-five GoldWave samples, and the crack that is the English |
| [08 — Clocks, crossings, predictions and calibration](docs/08-clocks-crossings-predictions-and-calibration.md) | seven clocks, zero crossings, fourteen corrections, five hunches scored, one term, rule 0 as a program, what is left |

## The rules this was written under

The object is not run, not installed, not emulated. Unpacking three
programs and a TSR by reading their stubs, decoding an FLC, rendering raw
pictures, splitting a text file and reading module headers are reading
bytes as data; FLC, S3M, RIFF WAVE, MZ and ZIP are public formats used as
such. **No outside source was opened to fill a cell** — not the owner's
"Polish or German", not any studio anyone half-remembers, not a wiki; what
the object does not print is declared not printed. Every figure names its
denominator and the command that re-derives it; every reader written here
refuses a directory, prints a non-Latin-1 name safely, selects by magic
and passes its selftest in a repository that does not hold the object.
The documents are in English; the session was in Italian.

# pc-hexxagon-doc

A measured description of one directory: twenty files, 1,297,836 bytes, holding
**HEXXAGON — The Animated Strategy Game** (Argo Games / Software Creations,
MS-DOS, VGA, 1993, ASP shareware, $20). The object is not published here. What
is published is what could be counted, decoded and checked.

## The short card

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **what it is** | a game: an Ataxx on a hexagonal board of 61 cells, for two players or against a light bulb in a bow tie called CRANIAC |
| **studio** | Argo Games / Software Creations, 26 Harris St., Clinton, MA 01510 |
| **year** | 1993 — from DOS timestamps written by a packer into a ZIP, independent of any file system |
| **platform** | MS-DOS, VGA (mode 13h), 286 or better, mouse and SoundBlaster optional |
| **files** | 20, in one flat directory, 0 subdirectories |
| **bytes** | 1,297,836 |
| **distinct sha1** | 16 — five board files share one hash |
| **mtime waves** | 6: four in 1993 and **two in 2005, written by the game while somebody played it** |
| **coverage** | specified 51.0804 %, derived 48.9196 %, **opaque 0.0000 %**, residue 0 |
| **the centre** | `GRAPHICS.HXG`, 626,424 bytes, 48.2668 %, 452 members, three compression kinds, **452 of 452 decoded** |
| **crossings** | 0 of 16 hashes over 110 repositories |
| **tools** | 582 Python files: 578 inherited, 4 written, 1 imported and attributed, 6 repaired |

**What this object has that no object here has had:** three independent accounts
of its own contents — a manifest the authors wrote, the self-extracting archive
it shipped as with a CRC-32 per member, and the files on disk. Twelve of the
thirteen members are byte-identical to what shipped. **And the manifest is wrong
about two of the twelve files it lists.**

**What was opened:** the HXG container and both of its compressors — a run
encoder and an LZ77 — from the bytes, checked against ten VGA palettes the
decoder was never told about. **What was not:** `HEXX.EXE`, which is under
LZEXE, and the reason is in [docs/06](docs/06-two-executables.md).

## The chapters

Twelve, and the count is the object's and not a convention. The two before this
one ran nine chapters for twenty-six files and ten for nine, so the number was
never the file count; here it is the number of things that turned out to be
separately true. Eight of the twenty files are prose, which is why four chapters
read documents and one of those is about not believing them.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [01 — HEXXAGON: twenty files, and half of them are paperwork](docs/01-what-this-is.md) | what it is, the denominator, and why a 51 % opening figure is not a compliment |
| [02 — The technical sheet](docs/02-the-technical-sheet.md) | every figure in this repository with the command that makes it again |
| [03 — The manifest, the archive and the disk](docs/03-three-accounts.md) | 12 of 13 identical by CRC-32, and the paperwork wrong twice |
| [04 — `GRAPHICS.HXG`](docs/04-graphics-hxg.md) | a directory that closes twice at zero, two compressors derived from the bytes, and why the author's own account of his format is not a specification |
| [05 — 1,690 bytes that count the game](docs/05-the-board.md) | 169 records, 108 sentinels, 61 hexes, and a hexagon of side 5 that fits a 320 x 200 screen to the pixel |
| [06 — Two executables, three packers](docs/06-two-executables.md) | LZEXE and PKLITE, a second specimen that refused for the wrong reason, and the decision not to unpack |
| [07 — `COME.SEE`](docs/07-come-see.md) | the advertisement that breaks the licence it travels with, and the classifier that called it Japanese |
| [08 — Five names, twenty dollars and an ombudsman](docs/08-the-credits.md) | what the paperwork says, and what it does not establish |
| [09 — Testimony and not measurement](docs/09-testimony.md) | the owner, his parents, and a strategy that turns out to be in the manual |
| [10 — The box](docs/10-the-tools.md) | four tools written, one imported, six repaired, and three selftests that broke on moving house |
| [11 — Corrections, and seven guesses scored](docs/11-corrections-and-the-hunch.md) | three right, one wrong, one half, two not settled |
| [12 — What is not measured](docs/12-not-measured.md) | the executable, the encoder, and seven words |

## The rules this repository works under

* **Nothing is executed, installed or emulated.** Decompressing is none of the
  three: `hxg.py` reads bytes out of a data file using a grammar derived from
  those same bytes, and no instruction from this object is ever run. The
  argument is made in [04](docs/04-graphics-hxg.md).
* **Every figure names its denominator**, and every figure has a command in
  [02](docs/02-the-technical-sheet.md) that reproduces it.
* **A figure written down by an interested party is a claim, not a
  measurement** — including a manifest written by the authors, which here is
  wrong on 2 of its 12 rows.
* **Sampling is declared.** Where a figure comes from a sample rather than a
  census, the tool prints "a SAMPLE" and the count.
* **Files are selected by grammar, never by extension.** This object contains
  three unrelated formats sharing `.HXG` and one `.ICO` that really is an icon.
* **Testimony is kept apart from measurement**, in [09](docs/09-testimony.md),
  including the place where it corrected this session.

## The tools

`tools/` holds 582 Python files and is published whole. Four were written here —
`hxg.py`, `hxgsave.py`, `pif.py`, `shipcheck.py` — and every one has a
`--selftest` that passes in a repository that does not contain this object, or
says how many checks it skipped and why. `pif.py` is
`pc-baronbaldric-doc/tools/pifico.py`, attributed in its docstring, imported for
the half this box lacked and brought up to this box's standard.

```
python tools/hxg.py       --selftest        35 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped
python tools/hxgsave.py   --selftest        29 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped
python tools/pif.py       --selftest        25 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped
python tools/shipcheck.py --selftest        23 checks, 0 failures, 0 skipped
```

# Leather Goddesses of Phobos — MS-DOS, Infocom, 1986

*Note: this game is an adult comedy. It carries a three-position explicitness
switch and its vocabulary and prose are explicit at the highest setting. This
document measures that switch and that vocabulary the same way it measures the
checksum — it neither quotes them for effect nor omits them — so a small number
of coarse words appear below and in `docs/`.*

A byte-level study of **fourteen files and 164,594 bytes**, in which a
twelve-kilobyte virtual machine differs from the one shipped with a different
Infocom title by **twenty bytes, all of them inside two filenames**; two story
files compiled a year apart share **67 of 96 abbreviations, 450 dictionary
entries and exactly 0 of 183 action numbers**; one in ten bytes of the object is
an installer designed to delete itself; and the only picture in the whole thing
is drawn with the alphabet.

This is the second Infocom object in this collection, and the first time it has
been able to ask a comparative question of the bytes rather than of the names:
**how much of an engine is engine?** The other object is the instrument, not the
subject — every chapter here stands on its own.

Nothing here is emulation, patching or preservation advocacy. It is measurement:
every number carries the command that reproduces it, the sixty-six predictions
were written before a Z-string was decoded and are scored whether they won or
lost, and every tool changed today was re-verified against the previous object as
a control.

**Nothing of the object is in this repository.** The fourteen files were copied
into this directory to be read, and `.gitignore` excludes them by directory name
before it excludes them by extension. `git ls-files` is verified line by line
before every commit. There is **one** piece of personal data in the object —
`readme.1st` is signed with a handle and ends with the name of a bulletin board
and a 1996 telephone number — and **none of the three is transcribed anywhere in
this repository, `notes/` included**. That it exists is recorded; what it says is
not.

The rule this document was written under, and the way it could have failed:
*having a control file, to write a document about the control instead of the
object.* The comparison is ten clauses of sixty-six and two chapters of
twenty-eight.

---

## The short card

| | |
|---|---|
| **title** | *Leather Goddesses of Phobos*, the MS-DOS edition. The object names its publisher in compressed text — `Copyright (c) 1986 by Infocom, Inc.` — and, unlike the previous Infocom object, **also in plain ASCII, eight times** |
| **platform** | MS-DOS, real mode. Three `.COM` files, two `MZ` executables, three `.BAT`; the game itself is not 8086 code but a **Z-machine version 3** program |
| **the object** | **14 files, 164,594 bytes.** One mtime for all fourteen: `1996-12-24T22:32:00Z` |
| **the date** | **1986-07-30**, from the header's `serial` field. The filesystem says 1996. **The product dates itself** — second document running where the year comes from a field and not a clock |
| **the layers** | story file **78.3886 %** · installer 11.5855 % · interpreter 7.2931 % · setup 0.9624 % · boss key 0.8554 % · Infocom's readme 0.3888 % · the uploader's note 0.5243 % · a 3-byte config 0.0018 % — and **no row marked unknown**. [20](docs/20-the-layers.md) |
| **the descriptor** | ninth answer to this collection's oldest question, and **the first repeat**: the same 64-byte header, the same byte-sum, declared `0xD070` and computed `0xD070`. Eight objects gave eight mechanisms because they came from eight *toolchains* — not eight objects. [03](docs/03-the-header.md) |
| **the interpreter** | 12,004 bytes, **20 of which differ** from the interpreter shipped with *Plundered Hearts*, and all 20 are inside `LEATHER.DAT` and `LEATHER.SAV`. The `F8 C3` that makes `Unauthorized copy` unreachable is **identical in both** — built that way, not patched. [05](docs/05-the-interpreter.md) |
| **the boss key** | `read.me` says CTRL-B. CTRL-B is character 2. The `cmp al, 2` the previous document could not explain opens `leather.scr` — a fake Cornerstone database screen whose menu offers `TOUCH`, `FONDLE` and `LUBRICATE`. **Neither story file emits character 2**: it is a feature of the machine that neither game knows it has. [16](docs/16-the-boss-key.md) |
| **the alphabet** | derived from the story file in five steps and checked against the 78 characters printed in the interpreter — **78 of 78** — with the caveat that those 78 bytes are inside the 11,984 the two interpreters share, so the check is no longer independent. ## The question

Two Infocom games, one year apart, on the same virtual machine, with the same
interpreter to twenty bytes and the same three-byte configuration file. Seventy-eight
per cent of each is compressed language.

**How much of that language is the same language — and where exactly does the
engine end and the book begin?**

**Sixty-seven of ninety-six abbreviations.** **Four hundred and fifty of nine
hundred and seventy-eight dictionary entries.** **Zero of one hundred and
eighty-three action numbers.**

And the shape of those three figures is not what it looks like. The compression
table is the most shared not because it is engine but because a ninety-six-slot
frequency table for English prose is almost entirely fixed by English; the
dictionary is less shared because it is four times larger and most of the extra
room is nouns, and nouns are the game. The shared fraction of a structure
measures how much of it the *language* already decided.

Which leaves one place where the answer is clean. At the action table — the first
structure whose contents are behaviour rather than English — the sharing is
**exactly zero**, and it stays zero for all 762 routines above it.

**The engine ends where the action table begins.** Below that line these are one
machine. Above it they are two books, and one of them is about Mars.

# Flight of the Amazon Queen — a measurement

A 1995 point-and-click adventure, written in Brisbane by two people, in its GOG
edition: **45 files, 237,605,368 bytes**, of which one file of **190,787,021
bytes** is the game and contains no index of itself. The table that says where
its **7,671 resources** begin and end is compiled into `scummvm.exe`, a free
program written by other people twenty-two years later, and there are **sixteen**
such tables in there. Five of the wrong ones describe this file with no hole and
no overlap.

This repository measures the object and does not run it.

## The three findings

**A table that closes arithmetically can be the wrong table.** Six tables inside
`scummvm.exe` describe `queen.1` with zero holes and zero overlaps, and five of
them are other countries' editions of the same game. The best-looking wrong one
covers 99.9703 % and leaves a 56,643-byte tail that looks exactly like a
discovery. It is the German CD's table, silently truncated at the first record
that would have run past the end of the English file. What separates the right
one from the wrong ones is not arithmetic but content: a `.PCX` begins with the
byte `0A`, and on the winner 128 of 128 do, and on every other table in the
executable, none.

**Eighty-nine per cent of a game can be one performance of it.** The recorded
speech is 170,238,763 bytes and four hours sixteen minutes; the whole written
work — logic, script, dialogue, cutscenes, credits — is 626,243, and the game's
own data file is 79,642. Delete the speech and the game still runs, with
subtitles, as it did on floppy a year earlier. Delete the 79,642 bytes and
there is nothing left but a stranger's voice.

**A descriptor reconstructed by strangers can be better than the original.** The
index in `scummvm.exe` covers this file at 100.000000 % with no holes, no
overlaps and no duplicate names, which is more complete than any descriptor this
collection has measured from inside an object. It is better because its authors
had a larger model: they were not describing this file, they were describing
sixteen editions at once, and that forced them to get every boundary right
sixteen times.

## Notes on method

Nothing here was executed — not ScummVM, not the installer, not the
uninstaller. Nothing was contacted. `PCX`, `ZIP`, `PDF`, `PE`, Standard MIDI,
Shell Link and the ScummVM `queen.tbl` record layout are public formats, used as
published and said so on each occasion; the sound container, the frame banks,
the AMOS banks, the depth masks, the light ramps and the music index were
derived from the bytes and each derivation is printed with the arithmetic that
closes it. The single number in this repository that is imported rather than
measured is the 11,025 Hz sample rate, which is named as imported everywhere it
is used.

Three identifiers belonging to the machine this copy was installed on are
counted and never written; `tools/leakcheck.py` reads all three out of the
object and proves that none of them appears in any committed file.

No decoded asset from the object is in this repository — no audio, no images, no
MIDI, no manual. The measurements are here; the game is not.

# Sam & Max Hit the Road — MS-DOS, LucasArts, 1993, Italian CD-ROM edition

*The repository is named `pc-samandmaxhittheroad-doc`, with `and` in place of
the `&`, because GitHub does not accept an ampersand in a repository name. The
title of the object is **Sam & Max Hit the Road**.*

A byte-level study of **sixty-four files and 227,198,319 bytes**, in which
**88.11 % of a CD-ROM is two and a half hours of Italian voice acting**, the
game that voice belongs to is one fourteenth of it, and the index that finds
them both is 9,080 bytes — one twenty-two-thousandth of the speech.

This is the first object in this branch for which a mature, free, famous
implementation already exists. **It was not used.** No line of it was read,
quoted, or consulted to check a result. Every structure here — the cipher, the
chunk header, the index record shapes, the string grammar, the image codec, the
font layout, the speech container — was derived from the bytes of this object,
and each derivation is written so that a reader can repeat it. Where a
structure could not be derived it is declared **not derived** rather than
filled in, and there is a list of those.

The derivations close. The container map owns all 13,789,910 bytes with zero
gap and zero overlap; the index resolves into it 566 times out of 566; the
speech container accounts for 100.000000 % of 200,190,289 bytes; 3,369
thirty-two-bit offsets extracted from encrypted scripts all land on the four
characters `VCTL` in a 200 MB file; 4,172 of 4,210 image strips end on their
own last byte; and 6,710,389 of 6,710,400 decoded pixels fall inside the range
their own code byte predicts.

**Nothing of the object is in this repository.** The sixty-four files were
copied into `CD/` to be read, and `.gitignore` excludes them **by directory
name before it excludes them by extension**, because two of them have no
extension at all. It was verified in both directions before the first commit.
`README.TXT` closes with the Italian distributor's street address, a
technical-support telephone number and a fax: **the company name is written,
and none of those three is transcribed anywhere here, `notes/` included.**

The rule this document was written under, and the way it could have failed:
*having a famous reader for the format, to write a document that quietly agrees
with it.* The check is that every claim carries the command that makes it
again, and every closure is described as a closure of **a** reading rather than
of the engine's.

# pc-kingsofthebeach-doc

**Kings of the Beach: Professional Beach Volleyball** — Electronic Arts, 1988,
MS-DOS. Measurements of an installed game directory, and the code to reproduce
them. **No game bytes are published here**: the hashes are, the files are not.

| | |
|---|---|
| files | **59**, one directory deep, no subdirectories |
| bytes | **524,839** — one denominator, not four |
| distinct sha1 | **55 of 59** (four collapsed hashes are four of the five 23-byte batch files) |
| form | **not a disc.** An installed MS-DOS tree copied off a hard disk: no image, no cue sheet, no ISO 9660, no sectors |
| dates | **1988-08-31 to 2002-01-29**, four separate hands, none of it a copy artefact |
| formats derived here | `.PAK` (36 files, 52.8225 %), `.DAT` (12 files, 16.7747 %), Microsoft EXEPACK (2 files, 27.8927 %) |
| format not derived | **0 bytes** |
| crossings with 117 other repositories | **0 of 55** |
| smallest object this pipeline has opened | yes — against 236,804,096 bytes for the smallest VIS disc |

It fits on a 720 KB floppy with 195,000 bytes to spare, and that is the method
rather than a footnote: on 524,839 bytes a four-byte needle has a chance rate of
0.0000, so for the first time here **a single hit is a finding and a zero is
evidence**. Three results rest on that, and the discipline that comes with it is
printed beside every count — a two-byte needle over 204,704 bytes is still
expected 3.12 times by chance and is still worth nothing.

## What is in it

* **a decompressor that produced exactly the right length and lost 11,184 bytes
  of code.** The toolbox's `exepack.py` unpacked both overlays to their declared
  `dest_len` with residue 0 and left the first 11,184 bytes as zeros, on both
  files. No arithmetic on the length can see that; the packer's own relocation
  table can. Repaired, controlled in both directions, and declared;
* **a magic number that was never a magic number.** All 36 `.PAK` files begin
  `0x82` and the program never compares anything to `0x82` — zero occurrences
  against a chance rate of 0.0000. It is the first *command byte* of a run-length
  stream, and the geometry everyone read as a header is the first two bytes of
  the decompressed output;
* **eight passwords stored as the one's complement of their uppercase ASCII**,
  four of which no published walkthrough names;
* **twenty-two names drawn in pixels**, which is why no string search had ever
  found them, and which settles two 8.3 abbreviations that would have been
  expanded wrong;
* **a Tandy build the loader offers on its own command line and that is not on
  the object**, with three of its four data files shipping anyway;
* and **four hands over fourteen years**, all of it out of one `find`.

## The chapters

| | |
|---|---|
| [00 — predictions](docs/00-predictions.md) | 70 clauses written before a byte was opened; 20 inherited, 50 open |
| [01 — the object](docs/01-object.md) | 59 files, one denominator, what it keeps and what it lost |
| [02 — the technical sheet](docs/02-technical-sheet.md) | every figure with the command that reproduces it, and the byte table that closes to 0 |
| [03 — what does not apply](docs/03-what-does-not-apply.md) | nine standard measurements listed rather than skipped, and two that invert |
| [04 — the programs](docs/04-the-programs.md) | a chooser, two EXEPACK overlays, and the hole the relocation table found |
| [05 — `.PAK`](docs/05-pak.md) | 52.8225 %, derived from the bytes; three tools refused first, one of them badly |
| [06 — the twelve `.DAT`](docs/06-dat.md) | 460 records, residue 0, and a mask whose height is the sum of two others on 70 of 70 |
| [07 — how it draws](docs/07-how-it-draws.md) | two overlays differing in one immediate byte, and a palette that reads wrong until you notice the monitor |
| [08 — how it sounds](docs/08-how-it-sounds.md) | an Adlib in 1988, a Tandy chip both builds drive, 39,624 four-bit samples |
| [09 — `VBTDY`](docs/09-vbtdy.md) | a build that is named, offered, and absent — and what the object cannot say about it |
| [10 — eight passwords](docs/10-passwords.md) | inverted ASCII, a menu entry, and five identical batch files that are somebody's notes |
| [11 — the people](docs/11-the-people.md) | twenty-two athletes, two authors in three spellings, and a fourth hand in 2002 |
| [12 — provenance](docs/12-provenance.md) | four strata, eighteen portraits in 166 seconds, two overlays ten seconds apart |
| [13 — protection and state](docs/13-protection-and-state.md) | two zeros, and only one of them is about this object |
| [14 — against the collection](docs/14-against-the-collection.md) | 0 of 55, and a checklist decision that reverses its own prediction |
| [15 — the tools](docs/15-tools.md) | 445 files, two written or repaired here, six defects on the record |
| [16 — leftovers](docs/16-leftovers.md) | eleven open items, each with the bytes that would close it |
| [17 — corrections](docs/17-corrections.md) | eight in the pre-briefing, four of mine, one sent elsewhere |
| [18 — the scoring](docs/18-prediction-scoring.md) | 20.00 of 20 inherited, 36.25 of 50 open, and the nineteenth calibration point |

Nineteen documents, following `pc-popcorn-doc`'s fifteen-chapter shape rather
than `pc-1000miglia-doc`'s twenty-two, with four added because three formats had
to be derived and one absent build had to be argued.

## The tools

`tools/` holds 445 Python files. 443 arrived from `pc-popcorn-doc`; two are new
here:

* **`tools/kotbpak.py`** — the `.PAK` reader, derived from the object's bytes.
  `--census`, `--validate`, `--refuse`, `--render`. Its refusal is controlled in
  both directions: 5 of 5 non-`.PAK` refused, and a real `.PAK` makes the control
  exit 1.
* **`tools/bytecross.py`** — copied from `vis-thesecretsofhoseafreeman-doc`.

and one was repaired: **`tools/exepack.py`** now restores the verbatim head and
runs a relocation check on every `--unpack`, exiting 1 when it fails.
`pc-popcorn-doc` produced this copy and the change matters to it — the
correction is in [docs/17](docs/17-corrections.md) with the command and the
offsets rather than the conclusion.

## Elsewhere

The row and write-up for this object were added to
[`pc-gamelist-doc`](https://github.com/vs-sr-dev/pc-gamelist-doc), commit
[`6e95b79`](https://github.com/vs-sr-dev/pc-gamelist-doc/commit/6e95b79986320371ad6339ee91ab7bedba91c29a).
Its year cell is the first in that index where the object contradicts itself in
two media and both halves are right.

The PC family has no shared platform checklist, deliberately.
[docs/14](docs/14-against-the-collection.md) asks with the count in hand whether
the **DOS-era subset** should have one — 24 of the 49 `pc-*-doc` repositories do
MZ header arithmetic and 16 meet a DOS-era packer — and answers yes, against its
own prediction, while declining to write it on the strength of one object.

## What is not here

`kings/` is in `.gitignore` in its entirety, and so is everything derived from
it. The rule was verified in both directions with controls that fire, and the
reason the directory is ignored whole rather than by extension is that three of
its fifty-nine files have no extension at all and two of those three are 70 KB
programs.

vs-sr-dev-pc-battlebugs-doc-readme.text:
# Battle Bugs (PC/DOS, 1994) — format documentation

Reverse-engineering notes for **Battle Bugs**, the tactical insect-warfare game
published by Sierra On-Line in 1994 and developed by Epyx — the last game Epyx
shipped before the studio wound down.

This repository documents the on-disk formats: the resource container the whole
game is built out of, the 16-colour planar image codec, the text tables, the
level layout, the sprite organisation, and the audio middleware. The compressed
image encoding was taken from the decompressor in `BUGS.EXE`, and
[docs/11](docs/11-disassembly.md) records the routine addresses so the claims can
be checked against the code rather than believed.

**No game data is included here.** The tools read a copy of the game you already
own. Every structural claim in `docs/` is re-checkable in one command:

```
python tools/bb_verify.py --dir /path/to/Bugs
```

which prints 59 PASS/FAIL lines against the real files.

*Published as is. These are reverse-engineering notes, not a specification: they are revisited and corrected over time, but no finding here is guaranteed to be complete or correct, whether or not a given section says so. What is marked open in [docs/10](docs/10-open-questions.md) is what is known to be unresolved, not the limit of what might be wrong. Prefer the verifier over the prose.*

---

## What was analysed

The **demo build** (`README.TXT` is titled `BATTLE BUGS DEMO`; `BUGS.EXE` is
dated 1994-07-14, 206,531 bytes). The retail build ships three additional
resource files that the demo omits but the executable still names — see
[docs/09-executable.md](docs/09-executable.md).

| | |
|---|---|
| Executable | Real-mode 16-bit MZ, **no DOS extender**, 1647 relocations |
| Extra memory | **EMS** (probes `EMMXXXX0`, `INT 67h`) |
| Video | **640×480 or 800×600, 16 colours, planar** (VGA mode 12h / VESA 102h) |
| Music | **XMIDI** (`FORM…XDIR`) through Miles Design **AIL** drivers |
| Digital audio | **DIGPAK** (The Audio Solution), 8-bit unsigned PCM |
| Configurator | Separate `BBCONFIG.EXE`, built with **Borland C++** |

## The interesting parts

**16 colours at 800×600, in 1994.** The obvious way to read "800×600" on a 1994
box is "expensive". The actual engineering is the opposite: by staying at 4 bits
per pixel and planar, a full screen is 240 KB of *video* memory the CPU never has
to touch as a linear framebuffer, and the mode is plain VESA 102h with a 640×480
mode 12h fallback that needs no VESA driver at all. The art budget, not the
resolution, is what 16 colours buys back.

**One asset set, two resolutions.** A full-screen background is stored as 40
tiles of 128×60 — exactly a 5×8 grid covering 640×480. Screens that also support
800×600 ship a *second* resource holding four bands: 800×60 top, 80×480 left,
80×480 right, 800×60 bottom. 640+80+80 = 800, 480+60+60 = 600. The higher mode is
the same picture with a frame drawn around it, not a different picture.

**A codec built around vertical runs and duplicate bitplanes.** The image
compression is per-bitplane, and within a plane it runs *down 8-pixel columns*
rather than along scanlines. On top of that, any bitplane identical to an
earlier one is stored as a single byte naming its twin — which is common in
16-colour art and is where most of the compression actually comes from. Both
choices are invisible from the outside and both defeat conventional RLE fitting;
[docs/10](docs/10-open-questions.md) keeps a note on exactly how.

**The radio.** Battle Bugs delivers its manual, its unit stats and most of its
jokes through an in-game radio with numbered channels. Those channels are 40
216×144 images in `CARDS` — unit stat cards, terrain cards for the food you fight
over (a Plop Tart™ has `HEIGHT: 2`, `CLIMBABLE: YES`), the command reference, and
parody TV listings for station **KNSX** (*The Lice Is Right*, *Dung Ball of
Fortune*, *Movie: Nesting with the Enemy*).

**A demo with the retail skeleton left in.** `CARDS` has 106 slots and fills 40;
`BUGS` has 44 sprite slots — 22 unit types × 2 sides — and fills 14. The empty
slots are two-byte stubs, so the demo is the retail layout with most of the
payload removed rather than a separately authored build.

## Documentation

| Document | Contents |
|---|---|
| [01 — File inventory](docs/01-file-inventory.md) | Every shipped file, size, role, and which are missing from the demo |
| [02 — Container format](docs/02-container-format.md) | The single offset-table idiom the whole game uses, and its nesting |
| [03 — Image format](docs/03-image-format.md) | The 9-byte header, the planar strip layout, and the compression |
| [04 — Video modes and palettes](docs/04-video-and-palettes.md) | Mode selection, the 7 palettes, the dual-resolution screen scheme |
| [05 — Text](docs/05-text.md) | `PERMSTR` / `TEMPSTR` / level-name tables and their three idioms |
| [06 — Levels](docs/06-levels.md) | Six-entry battle groups, terrain grids, object arrays |
| [07 — Units and sprites](docs/07-units-and-sprites.md) | The 22×2 slot map and the eight-facing mirrored animation layout |
| [08 — Audio](docs/08-audio.md) | XMIDI, the AIL/DIGPAK driver bundle, the sample banks |
| [09 — Executable and memory](docs/09-executable.md) | MZ layout, EMS use, the retail files the demo drops, `BBCONFIG.DAT` |
| [10 — Open questions](docs/10-open-questions.md) | Tile metadata, level records, and a note on how the codec resisted analysis |
| [11 — Disassembly notes](docs/11-disassembly.md) | Routine addresses in `BUGS.EXE`: decompressor, blitter, hit test, mode set |

## Tools

Python 3, `Pillow` only for rendering.

```
python tools/bb_extract.py list                   # container census
python tools/bb_extract.py strings                # PERMSTR + TEMPSTR
python tools/bb_extract.py levels                 # battle names + terrain grids
python tools/bb_extract.py render CARDS out/      # the radio channel cards
python tools/bb_extract.py --palette 4 screens out/   # 640x480 backgrounds
python tools/bb_extract.py --palette 1 tiles out/     # 396 terrain tiles
python tools/bb_extract.py --palette 1 sprites out/   # unit sprites, all facings
python tools/bb_extract.py raw SONGS out/         # 38 playable .xmi files
python tools/bb_verify.py                         # re-check the documentation
```

Point everything at your install with `--dir` or `BB_DIR`. Nothing in an image
record names the palette it expects, so `--palette` is yours to pick: 1 for the
battlefield and its units, 2 for the interface, 4 for the title screen.

## Status

Solved: container format, text tables, palettes, the image codec in both its
raw and compressed forms, the dual-resolution screen scheme, level structure,
sprite organisation, audio containers, executable characteristics.

Every image in the game decodes — 40 cards, 11 reassembled 640×480 screens, 396
terrain tiles, 1034 unit sprite frames.

Partly solved: the per-tile metadata trailers in `TILES.BIN`. The grammar is
settled — three items per tile, each either a six-entry block or a
back-reference — and 347 of 396 tiles parse; what the entries *mean*, and the
block-length rule that would resolve the rest, are not.

Still open: the coordinate encoding in the level object records, the sprite
parameter tables, and the `RECORDS.BIN` obfuscation. See
[docs/10](docs/10-open-questions.md).

# pc-cruiseforacorpse-doc

Measurements of **Cruise for a Corpse** (PC, MS-DOS, **Delphine Software
International**, 1991; English VGA 256-colour release) — not a disc image and
not a download, but **twenty files off somebody's hard disk in 1992**, of which
**95.2190 % is compressed** and had to be opened before a single string could be
counted.

Nothing was executed, no network exists in this object to contact, and no
decoded asset is shipped here. The 125 images and 1,095 members this repository
describes are reproduced from the object by the tools in `tools/`.

## The short sheet

| | |
|---|---|
| the object | `cruise-for-a-corpse\`, **20 files, 3,569,162 bytes**, no subdirectories |
| what it is | **`\DELPHINE\CR256`** — an installed game directory, and `READ.ME` names it |
| denominator | 3,569,162 bytes. The two 2013 PDF scans beside it, 10,077,320 bytes, are **out by declared decision** |
| coverage | readable **4.7810 %**, compressed **95.2190 %** — every string count is published against both |
| the containers | five volumes + an empty sixth, `24 + 32,880 + 3,424,605 = 3,457,509`, **remainder 0**, six negative controls firing |
| the compression | Delphine's backwards bit-stream unpacker, **848 of 849 with the format's own checksum at zero** |
| the one refusal | `D1/XX2.OVL` — **and it is the copy protection** |
| the payload | 3,424,605 → **14,086,466 bytes, 4.1133×**, 1,096 members, 867 names |
| the images | **63.6867 %**, and `.PI1` is **not** Degas Elite: two formats, `2 + 768 + 64,000` and `2 + 64 + 40,000` |
| the script | 80 `.FR` members, **76 English, 0 French**, and exactly **one** accented letter in 185,922 bytes |
| the music | **twelve Amiga Protracker modules with their sample data removed**, closing on 12 of 12 |
| **the thesis** | **0.6083 %** of this object is digitised sound — twelve 4-bit effects — against 4.0399 % of music that is instructions |
| the author | **nineteen names in plain text**, one member deep, behind the compressor |
| the company | **`Delphine` occurs 0 times** in 17.6 megabytes |
| build paths | **0**, at 4.78 % coverage and again at 100 % |
| protection | a **code wheel**, found in `XX2.FR`, not by a scanner |
| crossings | **0 of 888** distinct hashes against 71 repositories |
| clocks | **20 files, 20 distinct mtimes**, 1990-05-07 to 1992-07-13 — 797 days |
| the structure | **32 rooms + 6 close-up scenes**, bound by filename alone, and **9 members on all five floppies: the detective and the clock** |

## The four things this folder has to say

**One. The extensions lie, three times, and the object tells you so in clear.**
Seven `.FR` members are stored uncompressed and readable without any tool at
all, and they are in **English** — *"Paris, April 1927."* That is the warning. It
applies to `.PI1`, which is Atari ST's Degas extension on files that are **not
Degas** — a Degas `.PI1` is a fixed 32,034 bytes and nothing here is that size —
and it applies to the twelve extension-less members, which are **Amiga
Protracker modules whose instrument slots name `.AMI` sample files that this
object does not contain, with the first character of each name struck out with a
NUL byte.** The one place the Atari really survives is where nobody thought to
look: 56 of the 125 images carry a **12-bit Amiga/STE palette**, four bits per
gun, on a VGA card — while their pixels were converted to a layout the ST never
used. The colour is a fossil; the pixels are not.

**Two. The 95 % had to be opened before anything could be said, and behind it
were the names.** The four objects measured before this one in this branch all
hid their authorship in pixels, and the prediction written this morning said
this one would too. It does not. `D1/GEN.FR` and `D1/GENDEB.FR` are the credit
rolls in **plain text**, nineteen people under headings the game wrote —
`STORY CONCEPTION`, `MUSIC`, `QUALITY CONTROL`, `Special thanks to...` — and one
of those headings is **`CINEMATIC SYSTEM EVOLUTION II`**, which is this engine
naming itself, with a version number, in the product. The literature calls it
*Cinématique*; `Cinematique` occurs **0 times** here. And the company that made
it, published it, and gave this directory its name occurs **0 times too**:
`Delphine` is nowhere in 3,569,162 readable bytes or 14,086,466 unpacked ones.
`DELPHINE` occurs five times, in a readme, as a path.

**Three. One checksum fails in this object, and it is the one on the copy
protection.** 848 of 849 compressed members decompress with the format's own
running XOR landing exactly on zero. `D1/XX2.OVL` does not — and it decompresses
perfectly anyway: 8,185 bytes, write cursor on −1, source consumed to its first
byte, output a coherent overlay whose symbols are `combinaison`, `nb_essai`,
`tirage`, `fleche_h`. Its companion `XX2.FR` says `PROTECTION`, `Plug in the
combination`, `Incorrect code.`, and *"Put the wheel's arrow on the number you
have chosen."* Three bytes of one 32-bit word disagree with the value that would
close, and this repository does not claim to know which of three explanations is
right — only that the reader is not one of them, because the same code returns
zero on 848 others.

**Four. Fifteen per cent of this game is the same game written down five times,
and fourteen of its sounds do not exist.** 115 names ride on more than one
floppy so the player never has to swap disks mid-room: **544,071 bytes, 15.2437
%**, with `"INSERT DISK "` in `DELPHINE.LNG` as the receipt. Of those 115, 102
are byte-identical everywhere and **thirteen are not** — ten MT-32-shaped patches
edited between masterings in the same sixteen header offsets every time, and
three sound effects whose D2 copy is **one byte longer** than the D4 and D5
copies, the shorter being an exact prefix of the longer, because somebody
re-packed them and never updated the directory entry. Meanwhile the overlays
call for **29 distinct sound effects and the object contains 12**; fourteen of
the seventeen missing have no fallback patch either. The scripts came from a
machine that had those sounds. Five floppies did not.

## The chapters

| | |
|---|---|
| [00 — Predictions](docs/00-predictions.md) | written before the object was opened, wrong ones left standing |
| [01 — The object](docs/01-the-object.md) | what it is, the denominator, and why `READ.ME` describes this directory exactly |
| [02 — Technical sheet](docs/02-technical-sheet.md) | every number with the command that makes it again, and the **Engine** section |
| [03 — The volumes](docs/03-the-volumes.md) | the container, `VOL.CNF`, and 1,096 names crossed three ways |
| [04 — The unpacker](docs/04-the-unpacker.md) | the day's work: 95 % of the object, backwards |
| [05 — The images](docs/05-the-images.md) | `.PI1` is not Degas, and a person settled the pixel layout |
| [06 — Sprites, walkboxes and a font](docs/06-the-sprites.md) | `.SET`/`.SEC`, `.CTP`, `.FNT` — and what stayed shut |
| [07 — The script](docs/07-the-script.md) | English in a French extension, 616 names that check out, and the shape of the game |
| [08 — The sound](docs/08-the-sound.md) | the thesis: 0.6083 %, with the evidence against it |
| [09 — The protection](docs/09-the-protection.md) | a code wheel, and the only broken checksum |
| [10 — The executables](docs/10-the-executables.md) | three programs, two LZEXEs, and why `Microsoft` counts zero |
| [11 — The clocks](docs/11-the-clocks.md) | twenty files, twenty times, and no 1991 |
| [12 — The duplication](docs/12-the-duplication.md) | 15.2437 % spent so nobody changes disks |
| [13 — The author](docs/13-the-author.md) | nineteen names, and a company that is not there |
| [14 — Against the collection](docs/14-against-the-collection.md) | 0 of 888, and the seventh named engine |
| [15 — Leftovers](docs/15-leftovers.md) | 10 MB outside the numerator, and fourteen absent sounds |
| [16 — Personal data](docs/16-personal-data.md) | twenty names, all published by their owners |
| [17 — Corrections](docs/17-corrections.md) | nine in the briefing, eight of them mine |
| [18 — What was not done](docs/18-what-was-not-done.md) | the sprite table, the walkboxes, one 32-bit word |
| [19 — Scorecard](docs/19-scorecard.md) | two totals, because one total lies |

## The lists

* `notes/sha1-all.txt` — sha1, size and path for all 20 files
* `notes/members.csv` — all 1,096 members: volume, name, offset, packed,
  declared and produced unpacked size, and the sha1 of both forms
* `notes/images.csv` — all 162 `.PI1` entries with mode, dimensions and sha1

## The tools

Written this session, in `tools/`:

* `vol.py` — the volume reader, which refuses to list until the directory closes
  on the file, with six negative controls
* `unpack.py` — the decompressor, with six negative controls and a
  disagreement report
* `pi1.py` — the image reader, two modes and three candidate plane layouts, with
  six negative controls
* `frlang.py` — the `.FR` language classifier, with four controls
* `rooms.py` — the room families, the residency hierarchy and the `super.`
  global namespace, with ten controls

Everything else came from previous sessions and ran unmodified.
`iso9660.py`, `bank.py`, `cram.py`, `a3ds.py`, `avi.py`, `slack.py`,
`isoaccount.py`, `layoutbin.py`, `namecross.py`, `framediff.py` and `dates.py`
do not apply to a directory of floppy archives and were not used.

| identified | **91.4640 % of D1**, **95.4061 % of D2** |
| protection markers | 11 searched, **0 hits** over 32 of 32 files |
| entropy | first ever computed here; `golf.exe` at **7.9680** is the highest single file |
| predictions | 47 clauses written before opening anything; inherited **12.00 / 13**, open **26.50 / 34** |

## What this session opened

The container arrived already read — measured the day before on the VIS
pressing of the same game — and that was the constraint rather than the gift.
What had never been parsed:

* **`.PAT`, 153 of the 304 members**, the largest category: a 32×32 terrain
  mesh plus an object list, closing on **153 of 153**. It renders as Torrey
  Pines South.
* **`.BLK`, 80 members**, which the sibling repository declared unsolved after
  finding that *"no arithmetic tested closes on any specimen"*. Its row prefix
  is not a big-endian u16; it is two u8. **80 of 80**, 242 records, including a
  38-frame golf swing.
* **`.RS`, 36 members** with the magic `STEVE` and contents believed to be 8086
  code. A 70-level amplitude stream, settled by a member called `SILENCE` that
  is 499 bytes of a single value.
* **`.CEL` (9), `.COL` (3), `.OFS` (4)** — the last of which indexes the
  archive that contains it, **198 of 198 live slots landing on a node header**.
* **`title.lnx`**, whose fourth chunk the sibling repository filed as zero
  padding. It is the PC title screen's VGA palette, and it scores **2.87×**
  against that repository's own control, where the threshold is 1.5×.
* **`systype.exe`'s 30,200 unexplained bytes** — the payload of a 1989
  third-party self-extractor, named in the 1,510 bytes the header does declare.

## The chapters

| | |
|---|---|
| [00 — predictions](docs/00-predictions.md) | 47 clauses, written before any byte was opened |
| [01 — the object](docs/01-the-object.md) | what it is, two denominators, what it keeps and loses |
| [02 — the technical sheet](docs/02-the-technical-sheet.md) | every figure with the command that makes it again |
| [03 — the title screen](docs/03-the-title-screen.md) | the palette another repository filed as padding |
| [04 — the sound](docs/04-the-sound.md) | `STEVE`, and the member called `SILENCE` |
| [05 — the pictures](docs/05-the-pictures.md) | the span raster, and the field that was misread |
| [06 — the terrain](docs/06-the-terrain.md) | 153 members nobody had opened, and they are the course |
| [07 — the programs](docs/07-the-programs.md) | six MZ files, a 1989 self-extractor, a Microsoft driver |
| [08 — the documents](docs/08-the-documents.md) | a primary source, checked against the bytes, disagreeing with itself |
| [09 — the user state](docs/09-the-user-state.md) | the first in fifty-two objects, and it is somebody else's |
| [10 — against the collection](docs/10-against-the-collection.md) | two file crossings, 192 shared payloads |
| [11 — the scores](docs/11-the-scores.md) | 26.50 of 34 open, and what the six misses share |
| [12 — corrections](docs/12-corrections.md) | five mine, five for the sibling repository |
| [13 — leftovers](docs/13-leftovers.md) | 137,925 bytes that did not open |

`notes/` holds the two hash listings. `tools/` holds 426 Python files, of which
**nine were written here**: `lnx.py`, `cellras.py`, `cel.py`, `pat.py`,
`ofs.py`, `steve.py`, `palscoreraw.py`, `account.py` and `redactnames.py`.

## Privacy

Two of the thirty-two files are player records carrying names a previous owner
typed on their own machine, and **this game names the file after the string the
player typed**, so a directory listing publishes it. All 32 sizes and hashes
are published; those two names are replaced by `player-record-A.plr` and
`player-record-B.plr`, assigned in hash order. The reasoning is in
[chapter 09](docs/09-the-user-state.md) and the redaction is a tool that fails
loudly. Names their owners put inside the product they made and sold — the
title sequence's credits, and the corporate name — are published as published.

# pc-wackywheels-doc

Reverse-engineering notes on **Wacky Wheels** (Beavis Soft / Apogee Software, 1994) —
the DOS kart racer that is usually introduced as "the *Super Mario Kart* clone for the PC".

This repository documents the **shipped game data**: the `WACKY.DAT` archive, the
track and sprite formats, the fixed-point look-up tables that drive the pseudo-3D
floor renderer, and the save/config files. Everything here was derived from the
retail files of the GOG.com release (the original 17 Oct 1994 build, v1.1
"registered and upgraded"), not from any fan source reconstruction.

**Documentation only.** No game assets, no extracted art, no executable code is
committed here. The tools in [`tools/`](tools/) reproduce every figure and table
from your own legally obtained copy.

> There is a fan-made source *recreation* of Wacky Wheels in circulation. It is
> deliberately **not** used as a reference anywhere in this repo: the point of the
> exercise is archaeological — what the 1994 build actually contains, and what that
> tells us about how it was made.

## What is documented

| Doc | Contents |
|---|---|
| [00-overview.md](docs/00-overview.md) | Release, build chain, credits, content layout (42 track slots) |
| [01-wacky-dat.md](docs/01-wacky-dat.md) | The `WACKY.DAT` archive, including the two-byte offset bug baked into the shipped file |
| [02-graphics.md](docs/02-graphics.md) | PCX variant, `.SP` sprite banks, `SPRITE.ATR`, the `WxH.INF` pre-compiled scalers, fonts |
| [03-tracks.md](docs/03-tracks.md) | `.GAM .M .POS .PAR .SIN .RD .SPW` and the 2048×2048 tiled world |
| [04-engine-tables.md](docs/04-engine-tables.md) | `TRIG.DAT`, `SLP`, `VIEW`, `NDIST`, `MAP.XY`, `VEL*.TAB` — the renderer's LUTs |
| [05-audio.md](docs/05-audio.md) | `.MID`, `.KLM`, `.VOC`, `AUDIOT.FX`, the Apogee Sound System |
| [06-config-and-saves.md](docs/06-config-and-saves.md) | `WACKY.CFG`, `WACKY.ING`, `.HI/.TIM/.HTT/.OTT`, `WACKY.DTT`, `MODEM.PCK`, exit screens |
| [07-vs-mario-kart.md](docs/07-vs-mario-kart.md) | What is genuinely *Mario Kart*, what is genuinely *Wolfenstein*, what is neither |
| [08-open-questions.md](docs/08-open-questions.md) | Everything still unresolved, with the evidence gathered so far |
| [09-skunny-kart.md](docs/09-skunny-kart.md) | **Skunny Kart** (Copysoft, 1994): the bit-rotated `.LID` container, eleven byte-identical files, and the seven-cycle rename of the track extensions |
| [10-the-developers-account.md](docs/10-the-developers-account.md) | Andy Edwardson's first-hand history of the project, checked point by point against the shipped files |
| [11-other-kart-racers.md](docs/11-other-kart-racers.md) | Atari Karts (Jaguar, 1995) and Kart Race (DOS, 1996) run against the same fingerprints — both clear — and four independent answers to one rendering problem |
| [notes/wacky-dat-inventory.md](notes/wacky-dat-inventory.md) | All 577 archive entries |

## Tools

Pure Python 3 (`numpy` + `pillow` only for the rendering helpers).

```
tools/wwdat.py      WACKY.DAT directory reader / extractor
tools/wwpcx.py      the PCX variant used by the game (2 stray bytes up front)
tools/wwsp.py       .SP column-major sprite banks
tools/wwtrack.py    .GAM/.M/.POS/.RD/.SPW/.SIN parsers + world-texture rebuild
tools/wwtables.py   TRIG.DAT / SLP / VIEW / NDIST / MAP.XY / VEL*.TAB
tools/wwsaves.py    .HI / .TIM / .DTT record readers
tools/wwexport.py   one-shot: extract the archive and render every asset to PNG
tools/lidlib.py     Skunny Kart .LID archives (bit-rotated container)
tools/wwcompare.py  content-hash cross-reference between two extracted dirs
```

```sh
python tools/wwdat.py  "<install>/WACKY.DAT" extract ./out
python tools/wwexport.py ./out ./png

python tools/lidlib.py "<skunny>/SKUNNYK.LID" extract ./sk
python tools/wwcompare.py ./out ./sk
```

Chapter 11 runs two more kart racers of the period against the same
fingerprints — Atari Karts on the Jaguar and Mirinae's Kart Race on DOS — and
clears both, which leaves Skunny Kart as the only relative Wacky Wheels has.

Chapter 10 checks Andy Edwardson's own history of the project — the only
surviving first-hand account, given to the Apogee FAQ — point by point against
the shipped files. It corroborates most of what the bytes already said, and
resolves `DOPE.SP`: a 165 x 72 strip holding the Dopefish cameo, with
`BELCH.VOC` supplied by Joe Siegler, a microphone and a two litre bottle of
Diet Coke.

Also documented: **Skunny Kart** (Copysoft / Edisys, 1994). Its `.LID` archives
are obfuscated with a per-byte rotate-left-by-one; underneath, eleven files are
byte-identical to Wacky Wheels — including the incrementally generated
`TRIG.DAT` sine table with its characteristic drift — and the seven per-track
file extensions have been permuted by a single seven-cycle. Six of the seven
Wacky Wheels parsers read Skunny Kart's data unmodified; the seventh needed one
line, because Skunny Kart's descriptor inserts a sixth asset name. See
[09-skunny-kart.md](docs/09-skunny-kart.md).

## Status

First pass. The archive, the track data model, the sprite storage, the renderer
look-up tables and the save formats are solved and round-trip cleanly. The
`WxH.INF` scaler byte-code, `WACKY.SDX`, `*.BMC` and a handful of sprite banks
with non-factorable sizes are partially understood — see
[08-open-questions.md](docs/08-open-questions.md).

Wacky Wheels is © 1994 Apogee Software, Ltd. / Beavis Soft. Skunny Kart is
© 1994 Copysoft / Edisys SCRL. This repository is independent documentation and
ships neither.

# pc-1000miglia-doc

Measurements of **1000 Miglia** (MS-DOS, 1991–92), a simulation of the Brescia–
Rome–Brescia road race in its first seven editions.

**124 files, 1,588,227 bytes, one flat directory, no subfolders.** Not a disc
image, not a floppy set, not an archive: a directory as it sat on somebody's
hard disk. Every number below has a command in [tools/](tools/) that reproduces
it and a saved run in [notes/](notes/).

## What this repository measures, and what it does not

**It measures one installed directory.** Not the product. The distinction is
not pedantry — it is the largest single finding here, and
[05](docs/05-six-files-after-the-build.md) sets out the evidence: this folder is
one installation, made on 9 November 1992, of a **March 1992 bulletin-board
distribution** of a game that was finished on 11 February 1992. Two of its 124
files were written by somebody in another country, one more was compiled by
neither of the two compilers the game uses, and at least one file the program
requires is not here.

**It does not measure the studio.** The word `Simulmondo` occurs **zero times**
in 1,588,227 bytes, and so does every name the game is credited to. What this
folder shows about who made it, it shows in how it is built. The external
attribution is quarantined in [21](docs/21-leftovers.md) and used nowhere else.

> **Update.** That sentence is still true of *this* folder and is no longer the
> end of the story. A second Simulmondo object has since been measured with the
> same tools — [pc-simulman5-doc](https://github.com/vs-sr-dev/pc-simulman5-doc),
> *Simulman V*, MS-DOS, 1993 — and it names the company in full, in a
> corporate copyright line with a city and a country, and again in pixels on its
> title screen. **The two folders share one file, byte for byte:** this one's
> `MIDI3DRV.EXE` and that one's `NEWMIDIL.EXE` are the same 26,137 bytes,
> sha1 `cc4bf11d45eac6800d2739b2c341490981d1f1fa`, under two names a year apart.
> They also share the `.PAL` format, whose header grew from the two bytes used
> here to five there. The attribution for *this* object is still external and
> still quarantined; what has changed is that the studio is now attested inside
> the collection rather than only outside it.

**No asset from the material is in this repository** — only measurements and
the code that reproduces them.

## The four things worth knowing

**1. The sixteen filenames are a graph, and solving it gives the title.**
Sixty-four of the 124 files are sixteen groups of four named `ANRI`, `BLRO`,
`BOFI` … Read two letters at a time they are pairs of city codes over a
fifteen-node set, and the sixteen edges form exactly one closed circuit with
Bologna visited twice:

> `BS → PR → BO → FI → SI → BL → RO → SP → GU → TL → AN → RI → BO → PA → FL → VE → BS`

Brescia to Rome and back through Parma, Bologna, Firenze, Siena, Bolsena,
Spoleto, Gubbio, Tolentino, Ancona, Rimini, Padova, Feltre and Verona. The
answer to "what are these filenames" is the name of the game.
[07](docs/07-fifteen-cities.md)

**2. 37.93 % of the folder is an Amiga compressor with the bits the wrong way
round.** The seven `.FL` files are containers with a 128-slot directory and a
**signed** type byte — positive means stored, negative means packed, magnitude
is the format. The 235 packed members are PowerPacker 2.0, on DOS, in 1992. The
standard PP20 depacker fails on every one of them; what found the fix was a
MIDI file coming out ending `ff f4 00` where it had to end `ff 2f 00`, and 0xF4
is 0x2F with its bits reversed. All 328 members now read: **1,245,538 bytes out
of 602,478.** [08](docs/08-opening-the-fl.md) · [09](docs/09-the-bits-backwards.md)

**3. Three of the four size columns are one integer times a record size, and
the division has two answers.** `CT4 = 64n`, `POS = 386n`, `PTS0 = 122n + 18`
with `n ∈ {44, 49, 54, 59, 68}` — and an exactly-half solution, `32n`/`193n`/
`61n`, that fits the arithmetic just as well. The bytes kill it in one line:
`.POS` records are a two-byte header plus 64 `(x, y, z)` triples, and
`193 − 2 = 191` is not divisible by six. [06](docs/06-sixteen-by-four.md)

**4. The order is real, and it breaks in six places, and every break is the
same habit.** Sixteen groups with no gaps, five sizes and no sixth, 235
signatures matching 235 type bytes, an overlay and three IFF files closing to
the byte, fourteen palettes closing to the byte, zero odd second values in 124
FAT timestamps. Underneath: the first directory slot of all seven containers has
one stale byte, the map file writes fifty points per leg and never uses more
than thirty-nine, five bytes of 8086 are stuck to the end of a picture, and
every Pascal string in the folder still carries the tail of a longer one —
`Nuvolari` is followed by `rco`, which is the end of `Castelbarco`.
[14](docs/14-where-the-order-breaks.md)

## The documents

| | |
|---|---|
| [00 — Predictions](docs/00-predictions.md) | 102 clauses written before any measurement, never edited |
| [01 — Five hands, and the one that changed nothing](docs/01-five-hands.md) | 124/124 by SHA-1 and mtime against the original package; the `7z l` timezone trap, measured |
| [02 — This is not the product](docs/02-not-the-product.md) | what an installed directory costs, and the FAT parity check that says the clock is original |
| [03 — 124 files, 21 extensions](docs/03-the-census.md) | the census, the header agreement table, and the name that is not there |
| [04 — Sixteen months, forty-four evenings](docs/04-sixteen-months.md) | the dates at face value, and why this is the weakest chapter here |
| [05 — The six files after the build](docs/05-six-files-after-the-build.md) | an American disclaimer, a Scottish tracker module, a packed loader, and where this copy came from |
| [06 — Sixteen groups of four](docs/06-sixteen-by-four.md) | the integer, the rival solution, and the fourth file that has no formula |
| [07 — Fifteen cities, sixteen edges, one circuit](docs/07-fifteen-cities.md) | the graph, the decoding from the binary, and 1,616 bytes of map |
| [08 — Opening the seven `.FL`](docs/08-opening-the-fl.md) | the directory, the signed type byte, 328 members, 18 MIDI files |
| [09 — The bit order that was backwards](docs/09-the-bits-backwards.md) | one line of difference from the depacker everybody has |
| [10 — Turbo Pascal 6.0, and the `P` that is arithmetic](docs/10-turbo-pascal-six.md) | nine MZ files, three toolchains, one overlay, and a briefing corrected |
| [11 — Four tables, four layouts, one habit](docs/11-four-tables-one-habit.md) | 4,917 bytes holding everything the game declares |
| [12 — Two formats, three letters](docs/12-two-formats-three-letters.md) | `.ICV`/`.IMV`/`.CHV`/`.PAL`/`.CEL`/`.POL`, and ninety bytes of sky |
| [13 — Three files in a format somebody else invented](docs/13-somebody-elses-format.md) | the only externally-documented image format here, and it is loaded at run time |
| [14 — Where the order breaks](docs/14-where-the-order-breaks.md) | six defects, four of them the same one |
| [15 — What the program names, and what is not here](docs/15-what-is-not-here.md) | `INSTALL`, `MM.SAV`, and five utilities nothing calls |
| [16 — Against seven trees](docs/16-against-seven-trees.md) | zero by hash across 15,238 files; five shapes shared with the two DOS repositories |
| [17 — Is it a video game?](docs/17-is-it-a-video-game.md) | yes, in one word, and the question that replaces it |
| [18 — Open questions](docs/18-open-questions.md) | ten, each with what was tried and what failed |
| [19 — Prediction scoring](docs/19-prediction-scoring.md) | 48 / 25 / 28, and the four lessons |
| [20 — Tools](docs/20-tools.md) | 56 scripts: 18 applied, 36 that cannot be |
| [21 — Leftovers](docs/21-leftovers.md) | `w1n5t0n`, `LIPS.PAL`, and the external context, labelled |

## Reproducing it

Python 3, standard library only. The source folder is **not** in this
repository; supply your own copy at `1000 Miglia/`.

```sh
# the measurement that authorises the others
python tools/pkgdiff.py "1000 Miglia" _work/pkg/1000miglia/"1000 Miglia" _work/pkg/1000miglia

# the base census
python tools/census.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/headers.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/clockwork.py "1000 Miglia"

# the structure
python tools/groups.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/ptables.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/pictures.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/iffread.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/mzcensus.py "1000 Miglia"
python tools/refs.py "1000 Miglia"

# the containers, and 1,245,538 bytes out of them
python tools/flread.py "1000 Miglia" --extract _work/flmem
```

The folder name contains a space. Quote it. Python on Windows wants
`D:/...`, not `/d/...`.

## Provenance

The material was supplied as a plain folder, extracted from
GamesNostalgia's `1000miglia_dos_win.7z` (2,240,742 bytes, 135 files) with the
DOSBox wrapper removed. That removal was verified here and changed nothing:
**124 of 124 files identical by SHA-1 and by mtime, delta zero**. The person who
supplied it confirms that no copy of the original floppies exists in their
hands and that GamesNostalgia declared no source. Both negatives are recorded
in [01](docs/01-five-hands.md) as results rather than left as open questions.
