# pc-simulman5-doc

Measurements of **Simulman V** (MS-DOS, Simulmondo, Bologna, 1993) — the fifth
and last instalment of a cyberpunk adventure sold in fortnightly parts at
Italian newsstands.

**120 files, 2,056,643 bytes, twelve directories.** Not a disc image, not a
floppy set, not an archive: a folder as it sat on somebody's hard disk. Every
number below has a command in [tools/](tools/) that reproduces it and a saved
run in [notes/](notes/).

| | |
|---|---|
| files / bytes | 120 / **2,056,643** — the denominator for every percentage here |
| directories | 12 |
| distinct SHA-1 | 119 of 120 |
| distinct mtimes | **1** — `1996-12-24 23:32:00`, on every file |
| compressed or encrypted blocks | **0 of 557** |
| absolute build paths | **0**, over 100.0000 % of the bytes |
| recorded media | **0.0000 %** |
| unknown formats when this started | 16 |
| unknown formats now | 0 |

## What this repository measures, and what it does not

**It measures one folder.** Not the product: four fifths of *Simulman* was
sold on four other floppy disks and is not here, and the object says so in one
place only — the `5` in the name of a directory
([13](docs/13-what-is-not-here.md)).

**No asset from the material is in this repository.** No frame, no picture, no
MIDI, no line of the game's dialogue. Only measurements and the code that
reproduces them. `game/`, `_pre/` and `_work/` are all in `.gitignore` — the
object sits *inside* this repository's folder, which is new in this branch and
was the first thing verified, in both directions.

## The five things worth knowing

**1. The year is written in pixels.** All 120 files carry one identical mtime,
Christmas Eve 1996, which is wrong by three years. The string `1996` occurs
**zero** times inside the bytes. The game states its own date on its title
screen — `© FRANCESCO CARLA' 1993`, `© SIMULMONDO 1993` — drawn as
run-length-encoded artwork where no string search can reach it. It took a
decoder and a person looking at the result.
[04](docs/04-one-second.md) · [07](docs/07-fifty-eight-percent.md)

**2. One file is byte-identical to a file in the other Simulmondo game.**
`NEWMIDIL.EXE`, 26,137 bytes, is the same SHA-1 as *1000 Miglia*'s
`MIDI3DRV.EXE` — same driver, different name, a year apart. They also share the
palette format, whose header grew from two bytes to five between them, proved
by arithmetic on fifteen files at three different palette sizes. Beyond those
two things a racing game and an adventure by the same studio share **nothing**.
[06](docs/06-the-same-driver.md)

**3. 58.3509 % of the object is one format with no magic number, and it
opens.** A container whose first offset is the length of its own offset table,
a six-bit VGA palette, and a skip/copy sprite encoder. **156 pictures of 156**
decode consuming every byte but the two that mark the end — a count that went
from 0 to 156 when those two bytes were recognised for what they are.
[07](docs/07-fifty-eight-percent.md) · [08](docs/08-four-bits.md)

**4. The dialogue is XOR'd with a key stored in the file's own first byte.**
2,304 candidate transforms were tried; 96 cleared 85 % printable and 95 of them
were nonsense. The one that produced Italian is XOR with byte 0. The text
writes `_` for space 2,158 times against 3 — because the font's first glyph is
`0x21` and there is no glyph for a space — and its last glyph is `0x97`, which
is CP437's `ù`, the last letter Italian asks for.
[10](docs/10-one-byte-of-secrecy.md)

**5. Nothing in it was recorded.** No PCM anywhere; the music is nine MIDI
sequences with **zero program changes** in 13,825 notes, the timbres living in
12,345 bytes appended to the driver. The pictures are drawn. **0.0000 %** — the
second zero in that table, and the first one measured with the object fully
open rather than blind. [15](docs/15-is-it-a-video-game.md)

## The chapters

| | |
|---|---|
| [00](docs/00-predictions.md) | Predictions, written before the object was opened — 56 clauses |
| [01](docs/01-one-folder.md) | One folder, 120 files, and a denominator that had to be chosen |
| [02](docs/02-the-sheet.md) | The technical sheet: every number with the command that makes it again |
| [03](docs/03-not-the-product.md) | This is not the product, and it is the only thing here that knows what year it is |
| [04](docs/04-one-second.md) | Four clocks, one second, and a year written in pixels |
| [05](docs/05-two-compilers.md) | Four executables, two compilers, and the one with its source names |
| [06](docs/06-the-same-driver.md) | The same file, twice, a year apart, under two names |
| [07](docs/07-fifty-eight-percent.md) | 58.3509 %, no magic number, and 156 pictures of 156 |
| [08](docs/08-four-bits.md) | Four bits, the top sixteen colours, and a screen that is not scanlines |
| [09](docs/09-what-points-at-what.md) | A big-endian script, a graph that closes, and an index that does nothing |
| [10](docs/10-one-byte-of-secrecy.md) | One byte of secrecy, and a font that stops where the language does |
| [11](docs/11-nine-sequences.md) | Twenty-two minutes of music that never chooses an instrument |
| [12](docs/12-nineteen-bytes.md) | Nineteen bytes that reboot the computer |
| [13](docs/13-what-is-not-here.md) | What is not here, including four fifths of the product |
| [14](docs/14-against-the-collection.md) | One crossing, and a zero that meant nothing |
| [15](docs/15-is-it-a-video-game.md) | 0.0000 %, measured with the eyes open |
| [16](docs/16-three-names.md) | Three names, one criterion, two opposite answers |
| [17](docs/17-open-questions.md) | Open questions — six, and 3.06 % of the object unread |
| [18](docs/18-corrections.md) | Corrections — thirteen, four of them mine |
| [19](docs/19-prediction-scoring.md) | The predictions, scored: 42.0 of 56 |
| [20](docs/20-leftovers.md) | Leftovers: 227,721 bytes, 11.0725 %, counted exactly |

## Reproducing

```
  python tools/treecensus.py game
  python tools/mzcensus.py   game
  python tools/aniread.py    game                  # 156 pictures of 156
  python tools/eleread.py    game                  # 162 sprites, and the base
  python tools/plaread.py    game --tokens --graph # the reference graph
  python tools/keyread.py    game                  # the dialogue
  python tools/midread.py    game                  # nine sequences
  python tools/twosimul.py   game "<1000 Miglia>"  # the one crossing
  python tools/toolclass.py                        # all 278, or nothing prints
```

Add `--png <dir>`, `--copy <dir>` or `--dump <dir>` to write decoded material.
It goes outside the repository and stays there.

# StripPoker-1985

# fvf – decode, re-encode and repack the videos of *Star Trek: The Next Generation – A Final Unity*

`fvf.py` is a command-line tool for the **FVF** video format (Total Multimedia / SoftVideo) used by *A Final Unity* (MS-DOS, 1995).

| Command     | What it does |
|-------------|--------------|
| `info`      | Prints the size, frame count, duration and audio format of a video. |
| `decode`    | Converts a game video (`.fvf`) to an `.mp4` movie, a `.wav` sound file and, optionally, a folder of PNG pictures. |
| `encode`    | Builds a new `.fvf` from an original one. The new file has exactly the same size and identical audio. |
| `patch-zip` | Writes new `.fvf` files into a copy of the game's `STTNG.ZIP`, leaving every other byte unchanged. |
| `replace`   | `encode` followed by `patch-zip`. |
| `view`      | Opens the viewer in your web browser: play a video, or compare an original and a re-encode side by side. |
| `check`     | Scans video files and lists anything unusual (structure, codec features used, decoding errors). |
| `compare`   | Prints a report on how a re-encoded file differs from its original. |

Every command accepts `-v` / `--verbose` after the command name (for example `python fvf.py info -v FILE.fvf`) to print decoder header and block details.

**Tested in the game:** the re-encoded `teaser`, `title`, `warpout1`, `warnshot`, `labarriv`, `shiptour` and `tracbloc` videos play in DOSBox-X. `chodesc` was verified with the tool's own decoder and the viewer, but not in the game. The other videos were not re-encoded.

**Quality.** Re-encoding is lossy: the original files are already compressed, and the new file must have exactly the original size. Measured with `compare` (MAD = mean absolute difference per pixel and colour, on a 0–255 scale):

| Video | Mean MAD | Worst frame MAD |
|-------|---------:|----------------:|
| warnshot | 0.005 | 0.020 |
| warpout1 | 0.006 | 0.052 |
| chodesc | 0.018 | 0.134 |
| shiptour | 0.032 | 0.417 |
| labarriv | 0.068 | 0.165 |
| tracbloc | 0.099 | 0.290 |

In the viewer, the differences were not visible at normal size for any of these videos; a few single pixels could be seen when zoomed in on some frames of `labarriv` and `tracbloc`. Results depend on the footage, and the settings in section 5.3 matter for long videos.

---

## Contents

1. [What you need](#1-what-you-need)
2. [Set-up (Windows)](#2-set-up-windows)
3. [Get the tool](#3-get-the-tool)
4. [Get the video files out of the game](#4-get-the-video-files-out-of-the-game)
5. [Commands](#5-commands)
6. [Why `patch-zip` exists](#6-why-patch-zip-exists)
7. [The whole job from start to finish](#7-the-whole-job-from-start-to-finish)
8. [Troubleshooting](#8-troubleshooting)
9. [macOS and Linux](#9-macos-and-linux)
10. [Notes for developers](#10-notes-for-developers)
11. [Acknowledgements and licence](#11-acknowledgements-and-licence)

---

## 1. What you need

| What | Needed for | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| **Python 3.9 or newer** | everything | [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/) |
| **numpy** | everything except the viewer | `python -m pip install numpy` |
| **ffmpeg** | `decode` to `.mp4` only | Without it use `--no-mp4`; you still get the `.wav`. |
| **Pillow** | `decode --png` only | `python -m pip install pillow` |
| **A web browser** (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari) | the viewer | The viewer is one HTML file. It works offline and uploads nothing. |
| **The game's `STTNG.ZIP`** | `patch-zip`, `replace` and extracting the videos | About 650 MB (623 MiB). Keep an untouched backup. |

**Encoding needs time and CPU, not extra software.** It searches for the best way to store every picture.

- Measured on a Ryzen 7 7800X3D (16 threads): roughly 5–10 seconds per frame, for example about 40 minutes for a 286-frame video, about 78 minutes for 438 frames and about 3.5 hours for 2,265 frames.
- By default the tool uses half of your CPU threads (at most 8). More workers use more memory; if the PC runs out of memory, use fewer `--jobs`.
- You can stop with **Ctrl+C**. Running the same command again reuses the saved first-pass result (section 5.3).
- Do not let the PC go to sleep while encoding.
- `patch-zip` makes a full copy of `STTNG.ZIP`, so you need that much free disk space as well.

---

## 2. Set-up (Windows)

### 2.1 Open PowerShell

Press the **Windows key**, type `PowerShell` and press **Enter**. A window opens with a line such as `PS C:\Users\YourName>`. Commands in this README are typed after the `>` and confirmed with **Enter**. You can paste with a right-click.

### 2.2 Python

```
python --version
```

Any version from 3.9 up is fine. If you see `Python was not found` or `'python' is not recognized`, install Python from <https://www.python.org/downloads/>. **Tick "Add python.exe to PATH" on the first screen of the installer**, then close PowerShell, open a new one and run `python --version` again. (If `python` still fails, try `py --version` and use `py` in place of `python` everywhere.)

### 2.3 numpy and Pillow

```
python -m pip install numpy pillow
```

Pillow is only needed for `decode --png`.

### 2.4 ffmpeg (only for `.mp4` output)

```
winget install Gyan.FFmpeg
```

Close PowerShell, open a new one and check with `ffmpeg -version`. If `winget` is missing, download a build from <https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/> and add its `bin` folder to your PATH, or always use `--no-mp4`.

---

## 3. Get the tool

Copy the tool to a folder with a short path, for example `C:\FVF\FVF Tool`. The `fvflib` folder must stay next to `fvf.py`:

```
fvf.py
patch_zip.py
check_fvf.py
fvf_viewer.html        (the viewer; see below)
fvflib\                (decoder.py, encoder2.py, encoder3.py, encoder4.py, encoder7.py, recontainer_lite.py)
viewer_src\            (source and tests of the viewer; not needed to run the tool)
```

`fvf_viewer.html` is attached to each release. If you only have the source, create it with `python viewer_src/build_viewer.py`.

Open PowerShell in that folder (in File Explorer click the address bar, type `powershell`, press **Enter**), or type `Set-Location "C:\FVF\FVF Tool"`. Check that it works:

```
python fvf.py --help
```

Every command in this README is typed in that window. Put paths in **double quotes** when they contain spaces. A path starting `.\` is relative to the current folder.

---

## 4. Get the video files out of the game

The game keeps its videos in one archive, **`STTNG.ZIP`**, in the game folder.

1. **Back it up.** Copy `STTNG.ZIP` somewhere safe and never change that copy.
2. **Extract the videos.** Unzipping only reads the archive, so any program works: in Windows, right-click → *Extract All…*; in 7-Zip, open the archive and drag out the `.fvf` files you want.

Never put files back into `STTNG.ZIP` with an archive program; use `patch-zip` or `replace` (section 6).

The examples below use this layout. Replace the paths with your own.

```
C:\FVF\
    FVF Tool\             the tool
    Original\STTNG.ZIP    your untouched backup
    Videos\               the extracted .fvf files
    Output\               everything the tool creates
```

Create the output folder first (`decode` and `patch-zip` do not create it): `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\FVF\Output"`.

---

## 5. Commands

### 5.1 `info`

```
python fvf.py info "C:\FVF\Videos\warnshot.fvf"
```

```
C:\FVF\Videos\warnshot.fvf: 608256 bytes, 60 frames, 11 blocks, 4.0s @15fps, audio 1ch 8bit 22050Hz
```

A replacement file must have exactly this size.

### 5.2 `decode`

```
python fvf.py decode "C:\FVF\Videos\warnshot.fvf" "C:\FVF\Output\warnshot"
```

The second argument is a base name without extension. It creates `warnshot.mp4` (320×200, 15 frames/s, with sound) and `warnshot.wav` (8-bit mono, 22050 Hz).

| Option | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `--no-mp4` | Do not run ffmpeg; write only the `.wav`. |
| `--png FOLDER` | Also save every picture as `00000.png`, `00001.png`, … (needs Pillow; thousands of files for a long video). |
| `--frames N` | Decode only the first N frames. |

### 5.3 `encode`

```
python fvf.py encode "C:\FVF\Videos\warnshot.fvf" "C:\FVF\Output\warnshot_new.fvf" --work "C:\FVF\Output\work_warnshot"
```

The source must be an **original** game `.fvf`. The new file is written to the second path; use a different name from the original.

What happens:

1. The tool decodes the source, detects scene cuts and runs **pass 1**: it codes every frame at one common quality/size trade-off and records how many bytes each frame gets. The result is saved in the work folder (`need_slope.csv` and `need_slope_mad.csv`).
2. **Pass 2** codes every frame again with a byte budget derived from pass 1, using the real decoder in a closed loop.
3. The frames are packed into blocks so that the file is **exactly** the original size.
4. The tool decodes the new file with `decoder.py` and compares it with what the encoder intended and with the original audio.

Progress is printed and also written to `warnshot_new.fvf.log`. A line such as `file does not fit (short by 1234 B); lowering scale by 0.012 and retrying` is normal: the tool repeats pass 2 with a slightly lower budget until the file fits.

It ends with:

```
wrote C:\FVF\Output\warnshot_new.fvf 608256 bytes (target 608256 )
VERIFIED: decoder matches encoder model, audio identical; mean MAD ...
```

**If you do not see `VERIFIED`, do not use the file.** If the work folder already contains a pass-1 result, it is reused; pass 2 always runs again.

Common options:

| Option | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `--work FOLDER` | Folder for the pass-1 result (default: `OUT.work` next to the output). Use a separate folder for every video. |
| `--jobs N` | Worker processes. Default: half of your CPU threads, at most 8. `--jobs 1` runs serially. |
| `--redo` | Ignore a saved pass-1 result. Use it after changing the source file, `--pw` or `--lam0`. |
| `--mode s10` | Default. Two passes, best quality. |
| `--mode fast` | One pass, faster, lower quality; it can fail with "does not fit". |
| `--scale S` | Starting budget scale (default 1.0). It is lowered automatically until the file fits. |

Advanced options (the defaults suit most videos):

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `--need slope\|lossless` | `slope` | Pass-1 method. `slope` codes every frame at one common multiplier; `lossless` measures the bytes each frame needs to be coded without error. |
| `--pw W` | 2.0 | Key-frame persistence weight: static blocks of key frames count 1+W times as much (0 = off). |
| `--lam0 L` | 4.0 | Starting multiplier of the slope pass (it adapts). |
| `--floor F` | 0 (off) | Every frame gets at least this fraction of its original size; other frames pay for it. |
| `--floor-min B` | 0 | With `--floor`: frames planned below B bytes (nearly static frames) are not raised. |
| `--floor-mad M` | 0.03 | With `--floor`: frames whose pass-1 error (MAD) is below M are not raised. |
| `--protect P` | 0.97 | With `--floor` and a pass-1 error file: frames pass 1 codes almost perfectly keep at least this fraction of their planned size. |
| `--mad-tilt T` | 0 (off) | Byte-neutral: weight frames by (pass-1 error / 75th percentile) ** T so that frames pass 1 codes badly get more bytes. |
| `--mad-tilt-min X`, `--mad-tilt-max Y` | 1.0, 1.6 | Smallest and largest weight `--mad-tilt` may apply (1.0 means no frame is reduced by the weighting). |
| `--frame-cap B` | 24000 | Largest video chunk pass 2 may spend on one frame (the largest video chunk in the original files is 18,036 B; 25 of the 27 never exceed 18,008). |
| `--key-boost R` | 0 (off) | Byte-neutral: each key frame takes this fraction of the budgets of the three frames after it. |
| `--no-autoscale` | autoscale on | By default the starting scale is lowered until the packed plan is predicted to fit. This switch disables that. |

For a video with a long stretch that comes out visibly worse than the rest, a good starting point is `--floor 0.95 --floor-min 2500 --mad-tilt 0.2 --mad-tilt-max 1.4`. Compare per-stretch error with `compare` (section 5.8), not only the mean.

### 5.4 `patch-zip`

```
python fvf.py patch-zip "C:\FVF\Original\STTNG.ZIP" "C:\FVF\Output\STTNG.ZIP" "warnshot.fvf=C:\FVF\Output\warnshot_new.fvf"
```

Take the original zip, write a patched copy, and in it replace the entry `warnshot.fvf` with the given file. Give one `name=file` pair per video. The name on the left must match the zip entry exactly; the output must be a different file from the input. The new file must have exactly the size of the entry it replaces. The command takes about a minute.

It prints one line per replaced entry (the CRC values and offset depend on your files) and a final line:

```
patched warnshot.fvf crc XXXXXXXX (was YYYYYYYY) at offset NNNNNNNNN
done -> C:\FVF\Output\STTNG.ZIP 653379061 bytes (source 653379061 )
```

The two sizes at the end must be equal. If the command fails, the partly written output file is deleted.

### 5.5 `replace`

```
python fvf.py replace "C:\FVF\Original\STTNG.ZIP" "C:\FVF\Output\STTNG.ZIP" "warnshot.fvf=C:\FVF\Videos\warnshot.fvf"
```

Encodes every listed video (the right side of each pair is the **original** `.fvf`) and then patches the zip. It accepts the encode options of section 5.3 except `--redo`. Here `--work` is the folder that receives the new files and the per-video work folders (default `OUT.work` next to the output zip). Encoding can take hours, so for a first attempt run `encode` and `patch-zip` separately and inspect the result in between.

### 5.6 `view`

```
python fvf.py view
```

Opens `fvf_viewer.html` in your browser (or double-click the file). Files are read by the browser and never uploaded.

**To watch a video:** click **Open .fvf or .zip…** in box **A** and pick a `.fvf` (or `STTNG.ZIP`, then choose a video inside it; only uncompressed zip entries can be opened). Wait while the page analyses the video, then press **▶ Play** or the space bar.

**To check a re-encode:** put the original in **A** and the new file in **B**.

| Part of the page | What it shows |
|------------------|---------------|
| **View** buttons (keys **1**–**5**) | A or B alone, side by side, difference (the **×** box amplifies small differences) and wipe. **F** flips between A and B at the same spot. |
| Transport | Play/pause, frame step (arrow keys), one second (Shift + arrow keys), first/last frame, frame number, speed, loop, mute. |
| **Timeline** | A graph over the whole video: average error, brightness bias, worst pixel, share of pixels off by more than 8, bytes per frame, or change from frame to frame. Red ticks are scene changes. |
| **flagged ◀ ▶** (keys **[** and **]**) | Jump to the previous/next frame whose graph value is above the dashed line. |
| **This frame** | Bytes, flags, MAD, per-colour bias, worst pixel and share of pixels off by more than 8 for the current frame. |
| **Files** | Size, frames, blocks and decoding errors, plus three checks: same file size, same frame count, identical audio. |
| **Worst frames** | The 40 frames with the highest MAD. |
| **Save PNG** | Saves the picture currently shown. |

### 5.7 `check`

```
python fvf.py check "C:\FVF\Videos"
```

Accepts folders and files. It reads headers, blocks, frame records and every video instruction, decodes the video and prints a table and a list of warnings. It never changes a file.

```
file                 bytes frames blocks vid-max    raw%    8x8%   mv%   pal  warn   dec
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
warnshot.fvf       608,256     60     11   18008   53.8%    5.0% 11.4%     3     0    ok
5tharriv.fvf     2,596,864    261     44   18008   73.3%    2.1%  5.0%     8     0    ok
```

`vid-max` is the largest video chunk in bytes; `raw%`, `8x8%` and `mv%` are the shares of raw blocks, 8×8 transforms and motion-vector copies; `pal` is the number of frames with a palette; `warn` counts warnings; `dec` says whether the whole video decoded. `0` warnings and `ok` is a clean result.

| Option | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `--report FILE` | Write a detailed text report for every file. |
| `--csv FILE` | Write one table row per file. |
| `--no-decode` | Skip the picture decode (fast; structure and opcode statistics only). |
| `--deep` | Decode a second time with the picture buffers pre-filled with a different value and report differences. (The encoder assumes the buffers start as `0xAB`.) |

### 5.8 `compare`

```
python fvf.py compare "C:\FVF\Videos\warnshot.fvf" "C:\FVF\Output\warnshot_new.fvf" --csv "C:\FVF\Output\warnshot_compare.csv"
```

The first file is the original, the second the new file. Shortened output:

```
ORIGINAL warnshot.fvf: 608,256 bytes, 60 frames, 11 blocks
NEW      warnshot_new.fvf: 608,256 bytes, 60 frames, 11 blocks

Structure
  OK   same file size (required by the game)
  OK   same number of frames
  OK   audio identical in every frame
  OK   file header identical (apart from the last-block offset, bytes 20-23)
  OK   header last-block offset matches the new file
  OK   all blocks are multiples of 2048 and at most 63488

Video bytes by opcode class (share of all video bytes)
  ...

Picture error (new vs original): mean MAD 0.668, median 0.649, 99th percentile 1.313, worst 1.342
Brightness bias (new - original, green): mean -0.214, worst -0.492 at frame 19

Worst 15 frames by MAD:
   frame    time     MAD   R bias   G bias    max    >8 %  orig B   new B
  ...

Result: structure OK
```

(This example is from a `--mode fast` encode, which has a higher error than the default mode.)

- Every **Structure** line must say `OK`; `FAIL` means the game will not accept the file.
- **Video bytes by opcode class** shows what each file is made of.
- **MAD** is the mean absolute difference per pixel and colour; **bias** shows whether the new picture is darker or lighter overall.
- `--thr N` sets the MAD above which frames are listed as flagged (default: the larger of 1.0 and the 99th percentile). `--csv FILE` writes one row per frame.

---

## 6. Why `patch-zip` exists

The game is sensitive to how `STTNG.ZIP` is laid out, and ordinary archive programs change it:

1. **Entry order.** The game finds its videos through the zip's internal order. Archive programs reorder entries when files are added or replaced.
2. **Compression.** In the original zip the `.fvf` entries are stored uncompressed. Most archive programs compress what they add.
3. **Size.** Each `.fvf` must have exactly the size of the entry it replaces; that is why `encode` pads the new file to the original size and `patch-zip` rejects any other size.

`patch-zip` copies the original zip and overwrites the data of the named entries in place, updating only their CRC32 fields. Every other byte, every offset and the order of all entries stay the same. Always start from the untouched original `STTNG.ZIP`.

---

## 7. The whole job from start to finish

1. Set up (sections 2–3), back up `STTNG.ZIP` and extract the videos you want (section 4).
2. *(Optional)* `decode` an original and watch it.
3. `encode` each video and wait for `VERIFIED`.
4. Check each result with `compare` and the viewer (original in A, new file in B, use the flagged-frame buttons).
5. `patch-zip` to build the new `STTNG.ZIP`.
6. In the game folder, rename the old `STTNG.ZIP` to `STTNG.ZIP.bak` and copy the new zip in as `STTNG.ZIP`.
7. Start the game and watch the videos.

To go back, restore the original `STTNG.ZIP`. The tool never modifies your original files.

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
|--------------|------------|
| `'python' is not recognized` / `Python was not found` | Install Python with "Add python.exe to PATH" ticked, then open a new PowerShell. Or use `py`. |
| `numpy is required` | `python -m pip install numpy` |
| `No module named 'PIL'` | `python -m pip install pillow` (only for `--png`). |
| `FileNotFoundError ... 'ffmpeg'` | Install ffmpeg (section 2.4) or add `--no-mp4`. |
| `can't open file '...fvf.py'` | PowerShell is not in the tool's folder (section 3). |
| `FileNotFoundError: ... No such file or directory` | A path is wrong, or the output folder does not exist. |
| A path with a space breaks the command | Put the whole path in double quotes. |
| `invalid block size ... not a valid FVF file` / `bad magic` | The file is not an FVF video, or it is damaged. |
| `file does not fit (short by ... B); lowering scale ...` | Normal. Wait. |
| `cannot fit` | The tool gave up fitting the file. Do not use any output; keep the `.log` file. |
| The last line is not `VERIFIED` | Do not use that file. |
| Encoding seems stuck | Open the `.log` file next to the output in Notepad; it shows the latest progress line. Long videos take hours. |
| Out of memory | Use fewer workers (`--jobs 2`, or `--jobs 1`) and close other programs. |
| `patch-zip`: `size ... != archive entry ...` | The file does not have the size of the entry it replaces. Use a file produced by `encode`. |
| `patch-zip`: `zip64 archive: not supported` / `... is not stored` | The input is not the game's original `STTNG.ZIP`. |
| `view`: `fvf_viewer.html was not found` | Download the viewer from the release page or run `python viewer_src/build_viewer.py`. |
| The viewer cannot open a video inside a zip | Only uncompressed entries can be opened. |
| The game does not start, or videos are missing | Restore the original `STTNG.ZIP` and repeat with `patch-zip`; do not re-zip with an archive program. |
| The game stops loading a cutscene | Run `python fvf.py check FILE.fvf`; it reports a header byte 20–23 that does not match the last block. |

If a window closes immediately, you started it by double-clicking; always start from PowerShell.

---

## 9. macOS and Linux

The tool is plain Python. Install Python 3, numpy and (optionally) ffmpeg and Pillow with your package manager and pip (for example `brew install python ffmpeg` or `sudo apt install python3 python3-pip ffmpeg`, then `python3 -m pip install numpy pillow`; on newer Linux systems add `--break-system-packages` or use a virtual environment). Use `python3` instead of `python` and forward slashes in paths. The game itself needs DOSBox or DOSBox-X.

---

## 10. Notes for developers

- `fvflib/decoder.py` is the reference decoder. Importing it prints nothing; set `FVF_VERBOSE=1` (or pass `-v` to a command) for header and block details.
- `fvflib/encoder7.py` is the frame encoder used by `fvf.py`. It builds on `encoder4.py` (rate control), `encoder3.py` (block matching and opcode packing) and `encoder2.py` (constants and the temporal-skip builder). `recontainer_lite.py` builds frame records. `check_fvf.py` implements `check` and `compare`, and `patch_zip.py` implements `patch-zip`.
- Encoder behaviour can be changed with environment variables (read at import, so worker processes see them): `FVF_DIST=sad|sse|p15` (distortion measure, default `sad`), `FVF_CTX=0|1` (context-aware byte model, default `1`) and `FVF_COST_C5` (modelled byte cost of a motion-copy block).
- **Frame structure of the originals.** Frame 0 has flags 5 (decoded 16 times; it consists of 6000 affine blocks, about 18 KB). Every frame with index divisible by 4 has flags 4 (the buffers swap, so it becomes the reference); all others have flags 0 and predict from the last key frame. The encoder follows this structure.
- **Container rules the encoder follows.** Blocks are multiples of 2048 bytes and at most 63,488 bytes. The first block holds three frames (at most 61,440 bytes); the encoder puts at most six frames in each later block (the originals have up to seven). Header bytes 20–23 hold the file offset of the last block.
- **Tests.** The viewer's JavaScript decoder is a port of `decoder.py`. `python viewer_src/mkref.py FILE.fvf ...` writes reference hashes, and `node viewer_src/test_js.js FILE.fvf ...` checks the JavaScript output against them (needs Node.js). `python viewer_src/build_viewer.py` builds the single-file viewer from `viewer_src/viewer_src.html` and `viewer_src/fvf_decoder.js`.

---

- **The ScummVM project** and its contributors: the C++ FVF decoder reference was used as a second cross-check.

# Sherlock (ZX Spectrum, 1984) - annotated disassembly

A complete, cross-referenced, plain-English disassembly of *Sherlock*, the text adventure
published by Melbourne House for the ZX Spectrum in 1984 (developed by Beam Software), in
which you play Sherlock Holmes with Dr Watson and Inspector Lestrade over three days of
Victorian London.

It is written for people who **do not read Z80 assembly**. Every routine and every data
table has a title and a description, and the lines of every routine carry comments that
say *why* the line is there, in the game's own terms ("is the china man's disguise being
worn?", "the actor's own record") rather than restating the instruction or quoting a bare
address. Addresses in the text are links, so you can follow the code the way you would
follow a story.

**Browse it: open [`index.html`](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/index.html)** (or the published site, if you are reading
this on GitHub Pages).

## What you will find

| Page | What it is |
|---|---|
| [How the engine works](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/how-it-works.html) | The overview: actors and their scripts, the parser, the message language, the clock, trains and cabs. Start here. |
| [The case](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/the-case.html) | The story as the program holds it: the evidence flags, who must be cleared, and what Lestrade needs to hear. |
| [Walkthrough: Monday to the win](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/the-walkthrough.html) | One winning route, all 372 typed lines in 32 stretches, each with the clock, the room, the game's reply and whether the route still wins without that line. |
| [Every ending, played](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/the-endings-played.html) | The seven endings (one win, six ways to lose) and what you type to reach each. |
| [Map and rooms](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/map.html) | The room table drawn as a grid: exits, one-way exits, blocked exits and the garden maze. |
| [Pictures](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/pictures.html) | The 14 room pictures, drawn by running the game's own drawing routine. |
| [The cast and their scripts](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/cast.html) | Every character's plan script, decoded instruction by instruction, with where each one starts. |
| [Characters and things](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/things.html) | The object and character records and what the game does with each. |
| [Vocabulary](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/vocabulary.html) | The dictionary: every word the parser knows and what it means to the program. |
| [Trains and cabs](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/trains-cabs.html) | The timetables, fares and the cab ride. |
| [State bits](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/state-bits.html) | What "asleep", "dead" and the other bits in an actor's state mean. |
| [Bugs](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/reference/bugs.html) | 14 bugs in the original program, each explained. |
| [Trivia by theme](https://basf-c60.github.io/sherlock/trivia-by-theme.html) | 59 findings, grouped by theme. |
| [Routines and data](asm/) | The disassembly itself: 815 titled blocks, all named and explained, with about 9,200 line comments. |

## Things worth knowing about the game

A few of the things this work turned up, each explained in detail on the pages above:

- **Characters run their own programs.** Every character executes a small plan script each
  turn, in a little language of its own (verbs, "is it this hour?", "is this person in this
  room?", moves), using the same action code the player uses.
- **Messages are programs.** Text is stored as dictionary references and control codes: jump
  offsets, sub-messages, conditions such as "only if it is night", and a choice of
  sentence-ending punctuation. About 210 messages are rendered in full by running the game's
  own message printer.
- **It is a deterministic game with one random seed.** The random numbers step through the
  program's own bytes from a pointer seeded once at the first keypress, so an exact sequence
  of typed lines gives exactly the same game. A failed command costs part of a minute, and
  three failures in a row cost a whole one, which is why the timing of a route matters.
- **It can be won in two ways**, both by typing commands only: alone, and by shadowing
  Lestrade from Scotland Yard. The walkthrough page says which lines are essential and which
  can be dropped.
- **Bugs.** Fourteen are documented, including ones that were found by playing them.

## Repository layout

```
index.html, *.html        the browsable site (generated)
asm/                      one page per routine or data block
reference/                the Bugs and Trivia pages
images/, pictures/, maps/ location pictures, the map and the routine/message/data indexes
source/                   the sources the site is built from (see below)
tools/                    the build, check and analysis scripts
README.md                 this file
```

If you publish with GitHub Pages, note that Pages can serve only the repository root or a
`/docs` folder, so put the contents of the generated site in one of those.

### `source/`

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `game.skool` | The complete annotated disassembly in [SkoolKit](https://skoolkit.ca) "skool" format. |
| `game.ctl` | The SkoolKit control file it was generated from. |
| `game.ref` | The extra pages: overview, bugs, trivia, the case, the cast, the walkthrough and the rest. |
| `overlay_*.py`, `build.py` | The annotation scripts. Every description and line comment lives in these; `build.py` combines them into `game.ctl` and `game.ref`. |
| `sitegen.py`, `sherlock.css`, `linkify.py` | The page templates, the stylesheet (light and dark, phone-friendly) and the tool that turns addresses into links. |
| `rooms.py`, `gridmap.py`, `objects.py`, `dictionary.py`, `render_messages.py`, `walkthrough_steps.py` | Helpers that decode the room table, draw the map, list the objects, decode the dictionary, render every message with the game's own text printer, and build the walkthrough page. |
| `messages.json` | Every message in the game, as the game itself prints it. |
| `walkthrough_*.json`, `walkthrough_route_shortened.cmds` | The data behind the walkthrough page. |

## The version disassembled

The tape is the Melbourne House release `Sherlock v2.0`: a short BASIC loader
(`LOAD "" CODE: PRINT USR 32768`), a 256-byte loader stub, a 7,188-byte block at `$840B`,
the loading screen (6,912 bytes) and the main program block `p`, which is **41,600 bytes
loaded at `$5D80`** and runs to the top of memory. The disassembly covers the code and data
in the program block. The tape itself is not included in this repository.

## Checking the work yourself

You need [SkoolKit](https://skoolkit.ca) 10.1 or later (`pip install skoolkit`).

**Reassemble the disassembly and compare it with your own copy of the tape.** The result
should be byte-for-byte identical to the game's program block:

```
skool2bin.py -i source/game.skool rebuilt.bin
cmp rebuilt.bin p.bin && echo IDENTICAL
```

(`p.bin` is the main block taken from your own tape image; it is not distributed here.)

**Regenerate the website from the skool file:**

```
cd source
skool2html.py -d ../html game.skool game.ref
```

**Regenerate `game.skool` from the annotation scripts:** from the top level run
`python3 tools/check.py` (two or three times, until it stops changing things). It rebuilds
`game.ctl`, `game.ref` and `game.skool`, round-trips them through `skool2bin`, and checks
every address quoted in a comment against the real instruction boundaries.

## How it was made, and how far to trust it

Code and data were separated by running the game in a Z80 emulator and recording which
bytes were executed, then working out each table and subsystem by hand. Descriptions were
written from the code first, then checked:

- the whole disassembly reassembles to the original bytes;
- every address quoted in a comment is checked automatically against the real instruction
  boundaries;
- claims about behaviour were tested by running the game with typed commands, not only by
  reading code. The game has been **won from a fresh start with typed commands only (no
  pokes)** by two different routes, and every other ending that can be reached has been
  reached.

Things that were run are marked as such on the Bugs and Trivia pages, along with the ones
that are a careful reading of the code that was not reproduced. Testing also *overturned*
several earlier descriptions, and those were corrected throughout. For example, an early
note claimed the game could not be won; that was wrong and was withdrawn.

Some things are still open, and the pages say so where they matter:

- a handful of message stubs (the two-byte `WHAT` records) and one routine whose purpose is
  not known;
- why most lines in the winning route are needed. Any one of 39 can be left out and the game
  is still won, and the other 333 cannot, but whether each is needed for the story or only
  for the timing of the random numbers cannot be told apart with these checks;
- a few evidence flags and one state bit, listed on the pages that use them.

If you find something that is wrong, please open an issue. A corrected claim is worth more
than a tidy one.

## Credits and notices

- *Sherlock* is © Melbourne House. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by the
  authors, the publisher or their successors.
- This is a study of how the program works. A disassembly necessarily reproduces the
  program's code and data, so the same rights apply to it as to the original: it is
  published here for research and education, does not include the game tape, and should not
  be treated as a substitute for owning the game.
- The site is generated with [SkoolKit](https://skoolkit.ca) by Richard Dymond.

theruler-heroquest-dos-editor-readme.text: # HeroQuest Editor **An all-in-one editor for the DOS version of *HeroQuest* (Gremlin Graphics, 1991).** Edit text, quests, maps, monsters, furniture, graphics and sound effects of the original game files through a single graphical tool, with a live preview rendered with the game's own bitmap font. > Current version: **v6.8** — by **TheRuler** --- ## Table of contents - [Features](#features) - [Supported files](#supported-files) - [Screenshots](#screenshots) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Keyboard shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts) - [Building a standalone executable](#building-a-standalone-executable) - [Project structure](#project-structure) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Credits and legal](#credits-and-legal) A full step-by-step guide is available in **[MANUAL.md](MANUAL.md)**. --- ## Features ### General - **Automatic file detection**: just open (or drag & drop) a game file and the editor picks the right mode. - **Transparent compression**: `.BIN` and `.VGA` files are ompressed on load and recompressed on save. `.UNP` (uncompressed) variants are supported too. - **Unlimited Undo / Redo** for every editing mode. - **Unsaved-changes protection** when opening another file or closing the program. - **Drag & drop** loading (via `tkinterdnd2`, optional). - Dark UI, status bar with file information, and in-context hints for each mode. ### Text editing (language `.BIN`, `EQUESTS.BIN`, `INTRO.EXE`, `QUEST.EXE`) - **WYSIWYG preview** using the game's original bitmap font (`heroquest.fnt`) over the real in-game backgrounds. - Edit **scrolls (text boxes)**, **plain texts** and **button labels** of the five game languages (Italian, English, Spanish, German, French). - **Drag** text lines, buttons and whole scrolls with the mouse; **resize** scrolls with the corner handle; **double-click** a line to jump to its entry field; **add/remove** lines. - Full support for **accented characters** (à, è, é, ì, ò, ù, ñ, ü, ö, ä, ç, ¿, ¡ …) mapped to the game's own character codes. - **Search / filter** in the entry list. - Byte-budget counters where the original format has hard limits (e.g. the `INTRO.EXE` text area), so you never overflow the file. - Pointer-aware rebuilding: shared pointers are detected and shown (`×N` duplicates). ### Quest editor (`QUESTxx.BIN`) - **Mission briefing** text editor. - **Map editor** (26 × 19 board): paint tiles, whole rooms, walls and doors; door flags (**Opened / Secret / Fake**), wall flag (**Invisible**) and tile flag (**Revealed**). - **Monsters & Heroes**: drag monsters from the pool onto the map, move them, and edit each monster's **type, body, mind, movement, attack, defense and reward**; choose the **wandering monster**; place the heroes' starting positions. - **Furniture & Traps**: drag furniture (including multi-tile pieces and stairs with correct orientation) and traps onto the board; rotate/toggle orientation. - **Room events**: assign **treasure events** and **trap events** to rooms, with a visual map and tooltips. ### Graphics editor (`.VGA`, `.UNP`) - Full-screen **320 × 200** images and **multi-sprite** archives (monsters, heroes, furniture, sprites, …). - Tools: **Draw** (brush 1–10 px), **Flood fill**, **Rectangle select** with **copy / paste / delete / horizontal flip / rotate 90°**. - **Zoom** with the mouse wheel and **pan** with the middle button; right-click to **pick a color**. - **256-color palette viewer** and selector with built-in presets: *Default, Gremlin, Text 1, Pic 1, Hero 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7*; palette auto-selection by file name. - **Furniture groups** can be edited in a *composed* view; changes are applied to the right tiles. - **Import image** (PNG, BMP, JPG, GIF — quantized to the active palette) and **Export PNG**. - Paste images from the system **clipboard**. ### Sound effects editor (`.ALB`, `.RLD`) - EXPERIMENTAL - Browse the effects stored in **AdLib/OPL2 (ALB)** and **Roland MT-32 / GM (RLD)** sound banks. - **Play** an approximate synthesized preview. - **Extract** an effect as raw binary or as a WAV preview, and **import** a replacement effect. - The original bank structure is preserved when saving. --- ## Supported files | File | What you can edit | |---|---| | `ENGLISH.BIN`, `ITALIAN.BIN`, `SPANISH.BIN`, `GERMAN.BIN`, `FRENCH.BIN` | All game texts, scrolls and button labels (also `.UNP` versions) | | `QUESTxx.BIN` | Quest briefing, map, monsters, heroes, furniture, traps, events | | `EQUESTS.BIN` | Paged quest texts for all five languages | | `INTRO.EXE` | Intro texts and fixed system strings | | `QUEST.EXE` | Quest screen texts, position strings, DOS strings | | `*.VGA` / `*.UNP` | Full-screen images and sprite archives (`BOOK`, `BORDERED`, `FURN`, `GRAPHICS`, `GREMLIN`, `HERO1–7`, `INVENT`, `MAPS`, `MEN`, `MONSTERS`, `ODDS&SOD`, `PIC1`, `QUESTB`, `SHOPMP`, `SHOPSP`, `SPELLIT`, `SPRITES`, `TEXT1`, `WIZBACK`) | | `*.ALB`, `*.RLD` | Sound effect banks | > **Always work on copies of your game files.** Keep a backup of the originals. --- ## Screenshots --- ## Requirements - **Python 3.8+** with Tkinter (only if running from source). - [Pillow](https://pypi.org/project/pillow/) - [tkinterdnd2](https://pypi.org/project/tkinterdnd2/) *(optional, enables drag & drop)* A pre-built single-file `HeroQuestEditor.exe` needs nothing else. --- ## Installation ### Option A — Pre-built executable Download `HeroQuestEditor.exe` from the **Releases** page and run it. No installation required. ### Option B — Run from source ```bash git clone https://github.com//heroquest-editor.git cd heroquest-editor/data pip install pillow tkinterdnd2 python main.py ``` If Pillow or tkinterdnd2 are missing, `main.py` tries to install them automatically when running from source. --- ## Quick start 1. Launch the editor. 2. Click **LOAD** (or press `Ctrl+O`), or **drag & drop** a game file onto the window. 3. Pick an entry from the list on the left. 4. Edit on the canvas and/or in the panel below it. 5. Click **SAVE** (or press `Ctrl+S`) and choose the destination file name. 6. Copy the modified file back into your HeroQuest folder and test it in DOSBox. See [MANUAL.md](MANUAL.md) for details on every mode. --- ## Keyboard shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | |---|---| | `Ctrl+O` | Open file | | `Ctrl+S` | Save file | | `Ctrl+Z` | Undo | | `Ctrl+Y` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` | Redo | | `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` | Copy / paste selection (VGA modes) | | `Ctrl+H` | Flip selection horizontally (VGA modes) | | `Enter` / `Esc` | Confirm / cancel a pending paste (VGA modes) | | `Del` | Delete selection (VGA modes) | | Mouse wheel | Zoom (VGA) / scroll the edit panel | | Middle button drag | Pan (VGA) | | Right click | Pick color (VGA) · clear event (Room events) | --- ## Building a standalone executable The project is ready for **PyInstaller `--onefile`**. All resources are located at run time through `resource_path()` (which uses `sys._MEIPASS` when frozen). From the `data` folder just run: ```bat build.bat ``` or manually: ```bat python -m pip install --upgrade pyinstaller pillow tkinterdnd2 python -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --clean --onefile --windowed ^ --name HeroQuestEditor ^ --collect-all tkinterdnd2 ^ --add-data "heroquest.fnt;." ^ --add-data "background1.png;." --add-data "background2.png;." --add-data "background3.png;." ^ --paths . main.py ``` The result is `dist/HeroQuestEditor.exe`. Notes: - `--collect-all tkinterdnd2` is required to ship the tkdnd native libraries (drag & drop). - Some antivirus programs flag PyInstaller one-file executables as false positives. Use `--onedir` or whitelist the file if that happens. - To see error output, rebuild without `--windowed` and start the exe from a terminal. --- ## Project structure ``` data/ ├── main.py # Entry point, dependency check, window creation ├── config.py # Constants, palette, file lists, resource_path() ├── utils.py # Text codec, enc/dec wrappers, font loader, helpers ├── editor.py # Main Editor class: UI, load/save, undo/redo, mouse ├── editor_text.py # Text modes (BIN, EQUESTS, INTRO, QUEST.EXE) ├── editor_quest_map.py # Quest map / monsters / furniture / events editor ├── editor_vga.py # VGA image and sprite editor ├── editor_fx.py # Sound effects (ALB / RLD) editor ├── encoder.py # Game compression helpers ├── editor_lists.py # Left-hand list population and status bar ├── models/ │ ├── hq_bin.py # Language BIN files │ ├── hq_quest.py # QUESTxx.BIN │ ├── hq_paged.py # EQUESTS.BIN │ ├── hq_intro.py # INTRO.EXE │ ├── hq_quest_exe.py # QUEST.EXE │ ├── hq_vga.py # VGA images, sprites, palettes │ └── hq_fx.py # ALB / RLD sound banks ├── heroquest.fnt # Original bitmap font ├── background1-3.png # Preview backgrounds └── build.bat # PyInstaller build script ``` --- ## Troubleshooting | Problem | Solution | |---|---| | "Files missing" dialog at start | `heroquest.fnt` and the three `background*.png` must sit next to `main.py` (or be bundled with `--add-data`). | | "File unsupported" / wrong mode | Make sure the file is an original, unmodified HeroQuest DOS file with its original name. | | Drag & drop does not work | Install `tkinterdnd2`; when building, use `--collect-all tkinterdnd2`. | | Black console window flashes | Use `--windowed` when building; the editor already hides the `enc/dec` console. | | Game crashes after editing text | You probably exceeded a size limit: check the byte counters and keep texts within the original budget. | | No sound in preview | Preview uses `winsound` on Windows; on other systems it needs `afplay` (macOS) or a command-line player (Linux). | --- ## Credits and legal - Editor created by **TheRuler**. - *HeroQuest* is a trademark of its respective owners. The DOS game was developed by Gremlin Graphics. - This is an **unofficial fan tool**. It does **not** include any game data: you must own a legitimate copy of the game.
